title: [Audit] AV1 duplicate film-grain scaling points can panic and strand frame completion slots
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High (availability)
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/av1/src/header.rs:1251-1281](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/av1/src/header.rs#L1251-L1281) reads Y/Cb/Cr scaling coordinates without validating strict increase. [crates/av1/src/grain.rs:133-136](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/av1/src/grain.rs#L133-L136) computes `dx = xs[i + 1] - xs[i]` and divides by dx. Duplicate coordinates therefore divide by zero.

[crates/av1/src/decoder.rs:634-649](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/av1/src/decoder.rs#L634-L649) publishes picture/reference slots only after `decode_frame` returns. Slot::wait at lines 73-80 has no other completion path; dependent jobs and in-flight throttling (618-620) can wait forever after a worker unwinds.

## Conditions and realistic impact
An otherwise decodable displayed AV1 frame enables grain with duplicate adjacent scaling coordinates. Non-threaded decoding panics; frame-worker decoding can leave unresolved output/reference slots. The engine's synchronous panic guard does not guarantee completion of detached codec jobs.

## Recommended remediation
Reject duplicate/descending coordinates in header validation. Independently guarantee success/error publication for every submitted job, including unwinds, so dependents cannot be stranded.

## Suggested regression coverage
Malformed point ordering must return an error without panic. A bounded threaded test must verify both output and dependent reference consumers fini…

title: [Audit] AV1 tile-group parsing accepts duplicate coverage and accumulates duplicate tile state
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High (availability)
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/av1/src/decoder.rs:555-579](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/av1/src/decoder.rs#L555-L579) validates each group's numeric range but does not track prior coverage. Each tile payload is appended to `job.tiles`; non-final groups retain the pending job. On submission, parallel decoding allocates a TileState per accumulated entry at lines 759-767.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Repeated non-final groups accumulate duplicate tiles until a final group arrives. Skipped and out-of-order coverage is not rejected either. Small repeated payloads can induce much larger duplicated decode state and incorrect frame acceptance.

## Recommended remediation
Track expected coverage/order, reject duplicate/missing/out-of-order tile groups as required by AV1, and enforce a pending payload/state budget.

## Suggested regression coverage
At small dimensions, test valid partitioned groups plus duplicate, skipped and reordered coverage. Rejection must occur before unbounded accumulation or per-duplicate state creation.

title: [Audit] Matroska chapter and SimpleTag recursion is not depth-bounded
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High (availability)
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/matroska/src/meta.rs:244-275](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/matroska/src/meta.rs#L244-L275) recursively calls `parse_chapter` on ChapterAtom children; lines 295-308 recursively call `parse_simple_tag`. Neither carries a depth budget. Normal demux parsing ([crates/matroska/src/demux.rs:705-723](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/matroska/src/demux.rs#L705-L723)) checks metadata bytes but not tree depth.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Deep nesting inside an accepted-size metadata element can exhaust the parser stack. Recursively dropping accepted nested trees also needs consideration. A byte cap alone does not bound recursion, and stack overflow is not reliably recoverable by the command panic guard.

## Recommended remediation
Enforce depth and node limits before recursion; ensure accepted trees can also be destroyed safely. An iterative representation/parser is another option.

## Suggested regression coverage
Use small chosen depth limits in tests. Inputs just below/above the limit must succeed/reject deterministically, including cleanup after partial parse. Avoid attempting an actual stack-exhaustion run.

title: [Audit] Bitstream APIs have unchecked NAL endpoints and signed Exp-Golomb boundary errors
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High for 32-bit NAL parsing; Low for signed boundary handling
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
1. [crates/bitstream/src/lib.rs:314-330](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/bitstream/src/lib.rs#L314-L330) checks and slices using unchecked `i + len`. With a four-byte length prefix on a 32-bit/WASM target, the endpoint can overflow. `length_size == 0` also makes no cursor progress through nonempty input (direct API case).
2. `read_se` at lines 143-146 casts positive 2147483648 into i32 when the unsigned code is at its maximum. `write_se` at lines 218-220 overflows its u32 multiplication for i32::MIN.

The NAL helper is used by both H.264 and HEVC decoders.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A malformed declared length can cause arithmetic/slice panic on 32-bit targets. Unsupported prefix width zero can loop and grow output through the public API. Extreme signed values can decode with the wrong sign or panic/wrap when encoded. These are safe-Rust correctness/availability failures, not established memory corruption.

## Recommended remediation
Validate prefix widths and forward progress, use checked endpoints, and explicitly reject signed values outside the representation or widen that representation. Prefer error-returning APIs for invalid inputs.

## Suggested regression coverage
Native and WASM/32-bit tests for truncated/oversized lengths and unsupported widths; signed extrema and neighbors must round-trip or return documented errors in both debug/release configurations.

title: [Audit] Audio playback eagerly decodes whole files with no PCM budget or cancellation
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High (availability)
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/media/src/audio.rs:94-109](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/media/src/audio.rs#L94-L109),125-134,204-210 accumulates all decoded PCM in a Vec. [crates/media/src/player.rs:214-237](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/media/src/player.rs#L214-L237) starts decoding per cache miss; native jobs are detached and web decoding runs inline. Stopping voices at lines 294-300 does not cancel decode jobs, and cache entry count is not a byte/work budget.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Long clips or multiple distinct starts can consume substantial memory/work even after playback is stopped. One hour of stereo 48 kHz f32 PCM is approximately 1.38 GB before other buffers. Inline browser decoding can block UI progress.

## Recommended remediation
Stream PCM through bounded buffers, impose cache-byte and concurrent-job budgets, and support cancellation when decoding is no longer needed.

## Suggested regression coverage
Use a small budget and synthetic bounded sources to test long-stream handling, cancellation after stop/close, and repeated/concurrent starts. Verify actual retained bytes and work bounds rather than only successful return.

title: [Audit] Table split and selected-cell operations iterate unvalidated spans and rectangles
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High (availability)
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/model/src/table.rs:175-189](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/model/src/table.rs#L175-L189) loops over stored `row_span * grid_span`, checking cell existence only inside the loop. `normalize` at lines 194-201 only enforces a minimum span of one.

[crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:255-267](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs#L255-L267) accepts arbitrary selection endpoints. `cell_fill` at lines 198-218 constructs the entire inclusive Cartesian rectangle as a Vec before checking `cell_mut`. Selection clamping does not clamp cell coordinates.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A tiny imported table with oversized spans, or a programmatic out-of-bounds selection followed by fill, can cause enormous loops/allocations. Span-end arithmetic can additionally overflow on 32-bit targets.

## Recommended remediation
Validate/clamp spans and selected endpoints against actual table dimensions before work. Iterate existing cells without building an unbounded coordinate Vec, and use checked arithmetic.

## Suggested regression coverage
Tiny tables with oversized spans and selections must reject promptly without mutation. Cover 32-bit arithmetic boundaries, valid last-cell selections and normal merge/split round-trips.

**Severity:** Medium (availability/resource retention)
**Confidence:** High in allocation/retention defects; no OOM stress test
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
1. [crates/render/src/images.rs:116-121](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/render/src/images.rs#L116-L121) accepts up to 400 million pixels and calls `to_rgba8()` after decode. The image dependency DOES apply a default 512 MiB decoder allocation limit; that limit does not cover this subsequent conversion. A grayscale image within it can require about 1.6 GB additional RGBA output. Downsampling occurs afterward at lines 150-154.
2. Failed decodes insert strong source Arcs into `bad` at lines 144-147 (map declared at line 23). Successful pixmap eviction/accounting at lines 159-168 does not evict/account for failed sources.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Large low-channel images can exceed intended peak/output allocation budgets. Rendering successive distinct invalid/unsupported pictures retains their encoded buffers after closing the documents, for the cache's process lifetime.

## Recommended remediation
Check final RGBA and peak working memory before conversion, preferably dimensions before decoding. Bound negative-cache source bytes/entries or store bounded fingerprints rather than owning all failed inputs.

## Suggested regression coverage
With small budgets, reject conversions whose output exceeds the cap. Render/drop many invalid sources and verify eviction releases source Arcs. Retain valid decode/cache behavior as controls.

title: [Audit] RTL-language bidi processing repeatedly scans currency-sign suffixes, causing quadratic layout work
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High (availability)
**Confidence:** High; static causal analysis
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
New language-sensitive bidi code at [crates/text/src/bidi.rs:106-119](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/text/src/bidi.rs#L106-L119) processes each ET-class character independently. Line 114 scans `(i + 1..n).find(...)` through subsequent ET characters unless the preceding character is already numeric. A contiguous ET run with no adjacent numeric text leaves each character unresolved and repeats the suffix scan.

Normal layout supplies language flags to this function at [crates/text/src/lib.rs:827-834](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/text/src/lib.rs#L827-L834). Explicit bidi embedding controls use another path, but are not required for this case.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A long paragraph of currency signs such as dollar signs in a Hebrew/Arabic-language run produces approximately n(n-1)/2 class probes. Ordinary text input of modest size can therefore monopolize layout/rendering. No expensive workload was run.

## Recommended remediation
Resolve contiguous ET spans once or precompute next-non-ET positions, preserving language-specific bidi semantics with linear processing.

## Suggested regression coverage
Add public-layout coverage for long ET runs, numeric neighbors on either side, and mixed language boundaries. Use an operation/scaling bound rather than brittle wall-clock expectations. Existing short neutral-character tests do not detect repeated suffix scans.

author: PierrunoYT

title: [Audit] Inserting or deleting table rows and columns leaves merge topology inconsistent
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** Medium (content integrity)
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run. Any conditional or unverified manifestation is explicitly identified below.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/model/src/table.rs:109-140](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/model/src/table.rs#L109-L140) inserts/removes ordinary rows and cells without adjusting existing merge anchors, grid_span, row_span, h_merge or v_merge. normalize at lines 194-201 only makes rows rectangular and enforces minimum spans. The renderer skips covered cells, so orphan coverage is observable.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Insert/delete through a horizontal or vertical merge, especially delete the anchor row/column. Covered cells can remain without an anchor, or inserted cells overlap an unchanged span. This is separate from the unbounded span/selection work issue: valid ordinary edits also break topology.

## Recommended remediation
Make structural edits merge-aware: adjust spans, promote/rebuild anchors as needed, preserve intended text, and validate every covered cell belongs to a valid anchor.

## Suggested regression coverage

title: [Audit] MCP remote retries can execute non-idempotent commands twice after a lost reply
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** Medium (document integrity)
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run. Any conditional or unverified manifestation is explicitly identified below.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:58-71](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L58-L71) sends the request before reading its reply. Lines 76-91 reconnect and resend on any I/O error, including reply loss after execution. [apps/deckcraft/src/control_server.rs:42-53](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/apps/deckcraft/src/control_server.rs#L42-L53) only echoes request IDs; it does not deduplicate commands.

## Conditions and realistic impact
The app executes an insert/delete/undo or filesystem-related command, then the reply connection fails. The wrapper resends and the app executes it again. The client can report one successful call with two mutations.

## Recommended remediation
Use session-scoped idempotency keys with response deduplication, or do not automatically replay ambiguous non-idempotent calls: report outcome-unknown instead. Read-only queries can have a different retry policy.

## Suggested regression coverage
Use a fake server that executes once and drops the first response. Assert mutations happen exactly once, or the client returns an explicit ambiguous-outcome error without replay. Cover failure before connection as a safe retry control.

author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** Medium to High (availability)
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run. Any conditional or unverified manifestation is explicitly identified below.

Lines 164-171 scan all animations for each sequence; MAX_EFFECTS is checked only after matching that sequence at lines 173-175. ## Suggested regression coverage
Many distinct triggers, including beyond the effect cap, must preserve intended ordering with bounded processing. Verify work/scaling deterministically rather than relying only on a wall-clock timeout.

author: PierrunoYT

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/media/src/feed.rs:61-70](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/media/src/feed.rs#L61-L70) increments generation, sends Cmd::Seek, then blindly drains every queued message. The worker at lines 159-176 can process that new seek and publish new-generation frames/EOF before the drain finishes. The consumer's later generation checks in pull do not protect this earlier drain. At EOF the worker blocks for another command at lines 147-151.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A fast worker or short remaining clip can have its valid last frame/EOF discarded. The consumer then waits for data while the worker waits for another command, or starts playback after skipping the intended frame.

## Recommended remediation
Drain stale responses before dispatch where safe, or preserve/filter new-generation responses during the handoff. Prefer an explicit generation-aware seek protocol.

## Suggested regression coverage
Use deterministic worker barriers to publish a new-generation frame and EOF during seek handling. Both must reach the consumer; include stale queued frames and rapid successive seeks as controls.

**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run. Any conditional or unverified manifestation is explicitly identified below.

## Root cause and source evidence
[apps/deckcraft/src/audio.rs:58-59](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/apps/deckcraft/src/audio.rs#L58-L59) stores callback errors; reporting occurs during stop/drop (35-39,85-87). title: [Audit] Control server has no connection, request-line, or socket I/O resource bounds
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** Medium (local availability)
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run. Any conditional or unverified manifestation is explicitly identified below.

## Root cause and source evidence
[apps/deckcraft/src/control_server.rs:13-35](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/apps/deckcraft/src/control_server.rs#L13-L35) uses an unbounded request channel, spawns one thread for each accepted connection, and reads via unbounded BufRead::lines. Accepted sockets have no read/write deadlines. The 60-second timeout at lines 45-50 only bounds waiting for the UI response, not transport reading/writing.

## Conditions and realistic impact
When the optional loopback server is enabled, idle connections, oversized unterminated lines, or many concurrent clients can retain threads/memory and accumulate work. This is separate from authentication already tracked in #263; it is not claimed to be Internet-exposed by default.

## Recommended remediation
Limit simultaneous clients and request sizes; configure read/write deadlines and bounded queue backpressure. Authentication should be addressed through #263 rather than duplicated here.

## Suggested regression coverage
Small configured connection/line limits and deterministic idle/read/write timeout tests, including a blocked UI. Verify resource release on disconnect and overload without an exhaustion workload.

title: [Audit] Chart scientific number formats are interpreted as fixed-point precision
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** Medium (chart correctness)
**Confidence:** High; source-derived output, not runtime reproduced
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run. Any conditional or unverified manifestation is explicitly identified below.

New [crates/model/src/numfmt.rs:158-185](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/model/src/numfmt.rs#L158-L185) treats all digit placeholders between first/last digits as one fixed-point field. For `0.00E+00`, exponent zeros are counted as fractional digits, and E/+ are interior literals omitted by the final before/after literal emission at lines 198-209. ## Recommended remediation
Parse exponent notation explicitly, including mantissa precision, exponent sign and padding. Unsupported formats should use an explicit/documented fallback instead of silently folding exponent placeholders into fixed-point digits.

## Suggested regression coverage
Assert public axis_label/data_label results for scientific formats with small/large/negative/zero values and exponent-width variants, alongside existing fixed-point controls.

title: [Audit] Honeycomb transition geometry does not cover the bottom of a standard widescreen slide
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** Medium (visible transition correctness)
**Confidence:** High in geometric evidence; not rendered in this audit
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run. Any conditional or unverified manifestation is explicitly identified below.

## Root cause and source evidence
New [crates/anim/src/transition_fx.rs:794-811](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/anim/src/transition_fx.rs#L794-L811) computes row count using spacing rh*1.5 but places row centers at rh*0.866. Maximum settled vertical hex radius is rh*0.577. The background is black (line 798); late incoming cells never scale above one (818-831).

A read-only arithmetic check using a=16/9, rh=a/22 gives 11 rows and a last settled bottom coordinate <=0.746424 in normalized slide space. Thus the generated new-slide cells cannot cover the bottom quarter late in the transition. The endpoint special case returns a full slide at t=1.

## Conditions and realistic impact
An ordinary 16:9 slide with Honeycomb, near completion: a large lower region remains uncovered/black until the endpoint snaps to the full new slide. This is geometry coverage, not a subjective parity comparison.

## Recommended remediation
Derive row count from actual row spacing and hex extents, and validate full lattice coverage across supported aspect ratios. Check seams/column layout as part of the same mesh invariant.

## Suggested regression coverage
Assert late-progress triangle coverage across the unit slide including bottom/corners for 16:9 and 4:3, then inspect rendered late/endpoint frames. Existing finite-coordinate/mesh-count tests do not establish coverage.

title: [Audit] Asset audit slices UTF-8 at arbitrary byte offsets and misreads quoted Git paths
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** Low (audit-tool correctness)
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run. Any conditional or unverified manifestation is explicitly identified below.

## Root cause and source evidence
[xtask/src/assets.rs:70](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/xtask/src/assets.rs#L70) evaluates rest[..i] in take_while before checking is_char_boundary in any. A wildcard traversal through a multibyte character can panic. Lines 78-81 parse ordinary git ls-files output as literal filenames; Git-quoted Unicode/special paths then fail exists() and disappear from the asset check.

Unicode filenames can be silently skipped with normal Git quoting, or reach the invalid slice when paths are unquoted/passed directly to matching. Missing attribution can go undetected; matching can panic.

Use NUL-delimited Git output and actual filenames, and iterate valid character boundaries before slicing. Preserve support for spaces/newlines without display-quoting assumptions.

## Suggested regression coverage

author: PierrunoYT
body:

Validate all header invariants in from_head, or make invalid OpusHead values unconstructible and expose a checked constructor.

author: PierrunoYT

title: Smooth fade and slide transitions when switching ribbon tabs
author: Osaym
body:
### Description
When switching between tabs in the ribbon (e.g., Home, Insert, Draw, Design, Transitions, Animations, Slide Show, Review, View, etc.), the content currently switches abruptly with an instantaneous cut.

In Microsoft PowerPoint and modern Office interfaces, tab switching is polished and responsive:
1. The active tab indicator underline glides smoothly across the tab strip to the newly selected tab.
2. The ribbon panel content smoothly fades in with a subtle directional slide (entering from the right when moving forward, and from the left when moving backward).
3. The transition respects the application and system animation settings, instantly completing when animations are disabled.

### Expected Behavior
- Smooth cubic ease-out fade and slide transition on ribbon tab switches.
- Sliding accent indicator under the active tab in the tab strip.
- Instantaneous switch when animation effects are disabled in settings or headless test harnesses.

title: [Bug] Slide show: a first animation set to After/With Previous is skipped, the slide appears fully built
author: DavidPivert
body:
**Environment**

- DeckCraft 0.6.1, macOS universal DMG (tag `v0.6.1`, `688c7ef`), macOS 27.0.1 on Apple Silicon.
- The code involved is unchanged on `main` at `457406a`.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. New blank presentation, blank slide, black background.
2. Insert a white rectangle and give it a Fade entrance with **Start: After Previous** and a duration of 3 s
   (`animation.add={"effect":"fade","start":"afterPrevious","duration":3000,"ids":[<id>]}`).
3. Start the show on that slide: Slide Show ▸ From Current Slide, From Beginning, or → from the previous slide.

**Expected**

The rectangle fades in over 3 s as soon as the slide appears, without a click (as in PowerPoint).

**Actual**

The rectangle is fully drawn from the first frame, and `ui.inspect` reports `showing.step = 1` about 100 ms after the slide appears. With Previous behaves the same way. On Click works: the fade plays after the click.

| First animation | How the slide is entered | 300 ms | 500 ms | 1.5 s | 3.5 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| After Previous | `show.fromCurrent` | 255 | | 255 | 255 |
| After Previous | → from a slide without animations | 255 | | 255 | 255 |
| After Previous | `show.start` | | 255 | | |
| With Previous | `show.start` | | 255 | | |
| On Click | `show.start`, then → | | 52 (fading in) | | |

The automatic first step is started twice, and the second start finishes it:

1. [`ShowState::enter`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/688c7ef592c901ca4541c25e210c1b302e4dc066/crates/anim/src/show.rs#L123-L128) already sets `playing = true` when step 0 is automatic. title: Web build: run engine commands from the embedding page (a postMessage version of the control protocol)
author: MeetMellwyn
body:
**What**
Let a page that embeds the DeckCraft web build send it the engine commands the desktop app accepts on its control port (`engine.execute`, `engine.commands`, `document.inspect`), and get the results back, over `postMessage`.

**Why**
We embed the web build in a desktop app (Saxon Orc), so people can edit documents there while AI agents change the same documents with `deckcraft-cli`. Today the agent edits the file, and the open editor has to re-open it after every step. The view jumps, the undo history starts over, and the person has to stop typing while it happens. If the page could pass commands to the running editor, an agent's edits would land in the open document live, with undo, and both could work on it at once.

**Proposal**
It could follow GridCraft's `?host=parent` bridge (`apps/gridcraft-web/src/host.rs`). That bridge's `open` / `save` / `dirty` messages would be welcome here too.
- `deckcraft:execute` `{ id, command, params }` → `deckcraft:result` `{ id, ok, result | error }`: runs on the active document like `engine.execute` on the control port (one undo step per command, as on the desktop).
- `deckcraft:inspect` `{ id, text? }` → `deckcraft:result` with the `document.inspect` result.
- Only in host mode, and only from the same-origin parent window (as `host.rs` already checks), so other pages can't drive it.

We're happy to test it. Thanks for the editors!

title: CLI convert: .odp, .gif, .svg and .outline outputs silently get native .deckcraft bytes (exit 0)
author: Tokarzewski
body:
**Version:** deckcraft-cli 0.6.1, Windows x64 (the launcher's current build).

`deckcraft-cli convert IN OUT` picks the output format from OUT's extension. For `.odp`, `.gif`, `.svg` and `.outline` it exits 0, prints the output path and writes the **native `.deckcraft` bytes** under that name. Nothing says the format is unsupported.

**Steps**

```
deckcraft-cli run --sample --export in.pptx
deckcraft-cli convert in.pptx out.odp
deckcraft-cli convert in.pptx out.gif
deckcraft-cli convert in.pptx out.svg
deckcraft-cli convert in.pptx out.outline
deckcraft-cli convert in.pptx out.deckcraft
```

**Observed**

- Every command exits 0 and prints only the output path.
- `out.odp`, `out.gif`, `out.svg`, `out.outline` and `out.deckcraft` are byte-identical: 9,537 bytes, a zip (`PK\x03\x04`), the same SHA-256 (starts `e57d7719`).
- So a `.gif` or `.svg` that is really a zip, and an `.odp` that is not OpenDocument, are produced with no warning.

**Expected**

Either the format the extension names, or a non-zero exit with a clear error such as `unsupported output format .odp (supported: pptx, deckcraft, pdf, png, jpeg, ...)`. Silent substitution is the worst case for scripts, which cannot tell the output is wrong.

**Related**

- #210 covers the same pattern for `.potx` and `.ppsx`, which come out as plain presentations (I reproduced it: the main part's content type is `presentation.main+xml` for both).
- #163 is the same family for unknown `--flags` being taken as output names.

Found while generating test files headlessly with the CLI.

title: MCP reply validation accepts wrong IDs and buffered stale success
author: euisuh
body:
The remote MCP backend can use an unrelated reply as the result of a current mutation. This is pre-existing on main `457406a7a5b62425e915926c8ccb0984e61a198c` and also remains in #453; it is not claimed as a regression introduced by that PR or a duplicate of #409's lost-reply replay bug.

### Reproduction

1. A disposable loopback peer receives request ID1 and returns `{"id":999,"ok":true,"result":"unrelated"}` plus newline. The exact backend returns that unrelated result.
2. Against #453, send two newline-delimited response frames together. The extra success frame with ID999 is buffered in `BufReader`. On the next `engine.execute {command:"slide.new"}`, that buffered frame is consumed as success even though the actual current response is `ok:false`.
3. A valid JSON response followed by EOF without newline is accepted as a complete successful frame.

The tests use real production backend modules and synthetic loopback peers. They do not establish that a healthy application sends invalid IDs or execute any user's presentation commands.

### Source

Main [`backend.rs:92–96`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/457406a7a5b62425e915926c8ccb0984e61a198c/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L92-L96) and #453 [`backend.rs:117–121`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/d4cf50dd3d2e4c668d019405590ca663ca363b03/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L117-L121) inspect `ok` without checking the expected request ID. #453's [socket preflight](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/d4cf50dd3d2e4c668d019405590ca663ca363b03/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L60-L62) cannot see unsolicited bytes already held in `BufReader`.

### Expected behavior

Reject unexpected IDs/envelopes, incomplete or oversized response frames, and buffered unsolicited data before a new request. Drop the connection and report uncertainty once a request may have been transmitted. Do not replay the mutation.

Otherwise a faulty peer can shift results between calls and make an agent act on a false mutation success. Add re…

title: Timed-out control mutations remain queued and execute when the UI resumes
author: euisuh
body:
A control request reported as `timeout` can still execute later. This is pre-existing on main `457406a7a5b62425e915926c8ccb0984e61a198c` and is retained in #471; it is not a new bounded-queue regression.

### Concrete case

The control server queues `engine.execute {command:"slide.new"}` while the UI is not draining requests. After its 60-second wait expires, the client receives `{"ok":false,"error":"timeout"}`. When the UI resumes draining, the queued mutation is still dispatched. A user retry can therefore be followed by two executions; the old command can also act on a newly active document.

### Observed reproduction

A bounded harness using #471's exact control-server source sets its existing private test `reply_timeout` to30ms and deliberately leaves the test queue undrained. It observes the timeout reply, then retrieves the still-queued mutation. Its reply sender fails because the server has dropped the receiver. Actual later dispatch is established by the unconditional UI loop below; a full presentation app was not launched and no user data was changed.

### Source

- [Main server timeout](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/457406a7a5b62425e915926c8ccb0984e61a198c/apps/deckcraft/src/control_server.rs#L45-L51), retained in [#471](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/8dc068e0bacab1f058c17e270a1d7909ec02ac97/apps/deckcraft/src/control_server.rs#L152-L156).
- [UI drain](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/457406a7a5b62425e915926c8ccb0984e61a198c/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L1019-L1025) always invokes `control::handle` for received requests.
- [`ControlRequest`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/457406a7a5b62425e915926c8ccb0984e61a198c/crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs#L27-L37) has no abandoned/pending state.

### Expected behavior / smallest fix

Give requests a pending/taken/abandoned state. A timeout should abandon an unstarted request, and the UI should skip it. If execution already started, report an unknown outcome rather than a …

title: `normAutofit` without `fontScale` is shrunk on open, and the scale DeckCraft computes is not saved
author: vff
body:
**Environment:** macOS 15.7.4 (arm64), DeckCraft 0.6.1 (`deckcraft-cli`), compared with PowerPoint for Mac 16.113.4. `text::layout` is unchanged on `main` (d78e657).

Related to #327, but a different case: a body with `<a:normAutofit/>` and **no** `fontScale` attribute. #226 and #485 leave this case as it is, on purpose.

Both parts below have the same goal: DeckCraft and PowerPoint should draw the same file the same way.

**1. On open.** PowerPoint draws such a body at 100%, the schema default of `fontScale`, and does not refit it on open, even when the text overflows its box (#226 reports the same for saved scales). In the repro below PowerPoint draws the four lines at 40 pt, past the bottom of the box. On this machine DeckCraft shrinks them to about 11 pt (28%) to fit. In the PRs: #485 says "A 100% shrink still uses our own fit", and the `saved_shrink_scale_is_drawn` test in #226 asserts that text with `font_scale: 1.0` is shrunk below 0.9.

This matters because a master can carry the attribute. The template I hit this with has a bare `<a:normAutofit/>` on the master's title and body placeholders. Every slide placeholder that inherits from them and has overflowing text draws differently in DeckCraft and in PowerPoint, and the MCP `render_slide` tool shows the shrunk version.

With #226, the two cases could not be told apart: "no `fontScale` in the file" and "scale reset by `edit_text` after an edit" are both `font_scale: 1.0`. Keeping the saved scale as an `Option`, or setting a flag on edit, would let the first draw at 100% and the second refit.

**2. On save.** After an edit, DeckCraft draws the text shrunk, but the scale its layout computed is not stored in the model. The file is saved with `<a:normAutofit/>` and no `fontScale`, and PowerPoint then opens it at 100%. Storing in the model the scale computed when the text is refitted, so that the writer saves it as `fontScale` and `lnSpcReduction`, would keep the two in step.

title: `add_slide` puts the body in the first non-title placeholder of the layout
author: vff
body:
**Environment:** macOS 15.7.4 (arm64), DeckCraft 0.6.1, headless MCP (`deckcraft-cli mcp`). The code below is unchanged on `main` (d78e657).

`add_slide` (`slide.new` with `body`) puts the body text in whichever non-title placeholder comes first in the layout's shape order, regardless of its type, `idx` or size. The choice is made in `crates/engine/src/cmd/slide.rs`, in `slide.new`:

```rust
slide.shapes.iter_mut().find(|x| x.ph_type().is_some_and(|k| !k.is_title()))
```

The template I hit this with was exported from Keynote. Its "Title & Bullets" layout has a small subtitle-style body placeholder (`type="body" sz="quarter" idx="21"`, 73 pt high) ahead of the content placeholder (`type="body" idx="1"`). The body went into the small one, and the content placeholder stayed empty. The call succeeds, so nothing shows that the text went to the wrong box.

title: Feature Request: Custom AI Provider Module / Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) & Custom Endpoints
author: Ombiaxodin
body:
Currently, many modern productivity tools (like Microsoft PowerPoint with M365 Copilot, or various Claude/ChatGPT integrations) offer powerful AI capabilities, but they lock users into specific, proprietary ecosystems. ### Describe the solution you'd like
I would love to see a dedicated AI integration module that allows users to independently configure their own AI model connections. Specifically, the module should include:

API Key Field: A secure input field for users to provide their own API keys (BYOK).

Custom API Endpoint URL Field: An option to override the default API base URL. (e.g., pointing it to http://localhost:11434/v1 instead of [https://api.openai.com/v1](https://api.openai.com/v1)).

Model Name Input: A text field or dropdown to specify the exact model name being queried (e.g., llama3, mistral, gpt-4).

This would make the software compatible with any OpenAI-compatible API proxy, enabling seamless integration with self-hosted solutions like Ollama, LocalAI, vLLM, or LM Studio.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
Relying strictly on official plugins from commercial vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google). However, this creates vendor lock-in, incurs recurring subscription costs for the user, and prevents offline or privacy-first use cases where sensitive data cannot be sent to public cloud providers.

### Use Cases / Benefits

Data Privacy & Compliance: Corporate users or individuals handling sensitive data can use self-hosted open-source models without data leaving their local machine or company intranet.

title: [Audit] 2 crash defects with evidence and fix PRs: ASF probe arithmetic, ID3v2 tag-chain recursion
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Follow-up audit of the deckcraft media/IO path at `b1ca123` (current `main`). These two defects were listed in the earlier #727 audit, which closed when #728 landed — but the defects themselves did not land, and both are still present on current `main`. Per our audit practice, each finding ships together with its fix PR (regression tests included, red/green verified locally):

## 1. ASF probe walks objects with unchecked arithmetic — fix PR: #748

`probe_asf` (`crates/media/src/probe.rs:188`) walks ASF header objects with unchecked arithmetic: the loop guard is `while pos + 24 <= header_end` (`probe.rs:202`) and the advance is `pos += size` (`probe.rs:233`), where `size` is an uncapped 64-bit value read at `probe.rs:204`. A 64-byte file consisting of the ASF header GUID followed by 48 × `0xFF` makes `size = usize::MAX`, so the walk panics — `attempt to add with overflow` in overflow-checked builds, a slice-index panic after the wrap otherwise — and no such file can ever be probed.

Reachability: `probe()` (`probe.rs:50`) dispatches every ASF-labelled file to `probe_asf` (`probe.rs:55`), and the editor probes media on the UI thread (`ui-egui/src/media.rs:130`) whenever a file is inserted or played, outside any panic guard. The fix checks both additions so an object that overruns the header ends the walk (the correct ASF semantics), covered by the regression test `hostile_asf_object_sizes_end_the_walk`.

## 2. Chained ID3v2 tags recurse `Container::sniff` until the stack aborts — fix PR: #749

`Container::sniff` (`crates/media/src/lib.rs:76`) recurses once per ID3v2 tag: its `at(0, b"ID3")` arm (`lib.rs:94-99`) computes the tag size and calls `Container::sniff(b.get(10 + size..)…)` on line 97, so a file of N copies of a 10-byte empty ID3v2 header costs N stack frames — ~1 MB of crafted input is ~100k frames, past the main and worker stacks. The result is an uncatchable stack-overflow abort (SIGABRT), not an error: `Session::execute`'s `catch_unwind` guard cannot help,…

title: Boolean intersect blurs raster image output
author: earlvanze
body:
## Summary

After a boolean intersect operation involving a raster image, the resulting image is visibly blurred. The earlier issue #653 covered the operation failing or making the picture vanish; that issue is closed, while this is a distinct output-quality regression.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Insert a raster image.
2. Intersect it with a rectangle or text.
3. Compare the resulting image with the original.

## Expected

The intersected image retains its original visual quality except for the clipped area.

## Actual

The resulting image is visibly blurred.

## Evidence

The reporter supplied before/after screenshots in <https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/issues/653#issuecomment-6180051998>.

Related to #653.

title: Feature - Newtek NDI ingest/output from DeckCraft (or reimplementation)
author: gNovp
body:
(This issue is copied and adapted for each Crafting App where it fits)

It would be great to integrate directly into DeckCraft features from (or similar) to the Newtek NDI protocol, as described in https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issues/1569.

It is used today to capture and stream audio/video content with very low latency over a LAN, in scenarios like Digital Signage, Live video production, etc... And could be used to tie together even more the Crafting Apps

In DeckCraft, it's uses could be:
- Being able to output (expose) live presentation screen, and presenter view to other apps on the LAN/localhost
- Being able to ingest exposed sources from other apps on the LAN/localhost , via the existing Cameo function in PPT/DeckCraft.

Of course, as suggested in https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issues/1569, Newtek's NDI being free (moneywise) but proprietary, an open reimplementation shared between the Crafting Apps could be a better way as explained in the issue.

title: Text: an empty line inside a paragraph is sized by the first run, not by its own line break or paragraph mark
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**DeckCraft 0.7.0 windows-x64 portable, Windows 11 25H2, AMD Radeon Graphics** (`deckcraft-cli`; the layout code is unchanged on main 9859da3)

An empty line inside a paragraph (the line between two `<a:br/>`, or the last line after a trailing `<a:br/>`) is laid out with the font size of the paragraph's **first run**. PowerPoint sizes it by the mark that ends that line: the `a:br/a:rPr/@sz` of the next break, or `a:endParaRPr/@sz` on the last line. Every line below moves up or down by the difference.

Found in a real-world poster deck (one slide of 2384 × 1684 pt, six centred paragraphs with 88–133 pt text and 44–55 pt empty lines): from the second line on, the text drifts by up to 173 pt against PowerPoint's own export of the slide (SSIM of the whole slide 0.79). The deck can't be shared; the fixture rebuilds the pattern.

**Steps**

1. Fixture [`dc_empty_line_height.pptx`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/deckcraft/dc_empty_line_height.pptx): one 960 × 540 pt slide, four Arial text boxes (top-anchored, insets 0, single spacing, box top at y = 60 pt):
   - **A**: `A1` 40 pt · `<a:br>` 40 pt · `<a:br>` 10 pt · `A2` 40 pt
   - **B**: `B1` 40 pt · `<a:br>` 40 pt · `<a:endParaRPr sz="1000">`; next paragraph `B2` 40 pt
   - **C**: `C1` 20 pt · `<a:br>` 20 pt · `<a:br>` 60 pt · `C2` 20 pt
   - **D** (control): `D1` 40 pt; an empty paragraph with `<a:endParaRPr sz="1000">`; `D2` 40 pt
2. `deckcraft-cli render dc_empty_line_height.pptx --slide 1 --scale 1 out.png`
3. Measure the top of the ink of the first and the second text line in each box (1 px = 1 pt).

**Expected** (PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 on Windows, the same slide exported at 1 px per pt) and **Actual** (DeckCraft 0.7.0):

title: CLI/MCP format.font changes only Latin typeface; expose East Asian and complex-script font controls
author: yx15713668358-bot
body:
## Observed behavior

In DeckCraft 0.7.0 (macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon), `format.font` updates the Latin `font` property but leaves existing `font_ea` and `font_cs` properties unchanged. Saving to PPTX therefore leaves the previous `<a:ea>` and `<a:cs>` typeface names even after selecting a new CJK-capable family through the CLI/MCP.

This matters for imported CJK presentations: the editor can look correct while the serialized PPTX still asks another viewer to use the old East Asian font.

## Reproduction

1. Open a PPTX containing a text run with explicit Latin and East Asian typefaces. A minimal starting run is:

```xml
<a:rPr><a:latin typeface="Old Latin"/><a:ea typeface="PingFang SC"/><a:cs typeface="PingFang SC"/></a:rPr>
```

2. Select that text shape and execute the existing command through CLI/MCP:

```json
{"command":"format.font","params":{"family":"Noto Sans CJK SC"}}
```

3. Save the PPTX and inspect `ppt/slides/slide1.xml`.

Actual: `<a:latin typeface="Noto Sans CJK SC"/>` changes, but `<a:ea typeface="PingFang SC"/>` and `<a:cs .../>` remain.

Expected: provide an explicit supported way to set East Asian and complex-script families, or clearly document the Latin-only behavior. An explicit optional parameter would preserve the existing command semantics.

## Source check

The current default-branch implementation was checked before filing: [`font()` in crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/main/crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs) still assigns only `r.font`. The model already contains `font_ea` and `font_cs`.

## Locally tested API extension

A local build of 0.7.0 adds optional parameters without changing the existing Latin-only call:

```json
{"command":"format.font","params":{"family":"Noto Sans CJK SC","eastAsia":"Noto Sans CJK SC","complexScript":"Noto Sans CJK SC"}}
```

title: Browse for Themes applies only the theme, not the template's slide master and layouts
author: Faabyy
body:
## Problem

There's no way to apply a slide master (a company template, say) to a presentation that already exists.

In PowerPoint this is **Design › Themes › Browse for Themes…**: picking a `.potx`, `.pptx` or `.thmx` brings in that file's **slide master and its layouts** (background, master graphics such as a logo, placeholder positions, title and body text styles, footers) along with the theme. Existing slides are then mapped onto the new layouts by layout type, so their content takes the new look.

DeckCraft's Browse for Themes… (`design.browseTheme`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/design.rs`) only replaces the **theme part** of the current master (`m.theme = theme`): colours, fonts and effects. The master's shapes, backgrounds, text styles and layouts stay as they were, so a corporate template can't be applied to an existing deck.

The other ways around it don't help either:

- **Reuse Slides (Keep Source Formatting)** brings the source master, but only together with the source's slides. You can't move your own slides onto it.
- **Slide Master view** has `master.insertLayout`, `deleteLayout`, `renameLayout`, `insertPlaceholder`, `preserve` and `placeholders`, but no way to insert a master from another file.

## Docs disagree

- `docs/parity-checklist.md:105`: "Browse themes from .pptx/.thmx" is marked **D** (done).
- `docs/file-format-parity.md:25`: `.thmx` reads "no / no — Browse for themes is a P2 row".
- `docs/gaps.md` doesn't mention it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Make a template: in Slide Master view, put a logo and a coloured background on the master and move the title placeholder. Save it as `Brand.potx`.
2. Open another deck with a few title and content slides.
3. Design › Browse for Themes…, pick `Brand.potx`.

**Expected (PowerPoint):** the slides take the template's master and layouts: logo, background, placeholder positions, text styles, plus its colours and fonts.
**Actual:** only the colours, fonts and effects change.

Follow Power…

title: CLI convert to .txt / .md leaves out all table text (exit 0, no warning)
author: zengbo
body:
**Version:** deckcraft-cli 0.7.0 (release tarball `deckcraft-0.7.0-linux-aarch64.tar.gz`), Ubuntu, aarch64

**What happens**

`deckcraft-cli convert deck.pptx out.txt` (and `out.md`) writes the text of titles and text boxes but leaves out every table cell. The command exits 0 with no warning, so a reader of the export cannot tell that content is missing. The table itself is kept on a `.pptx` save and renders in `render`/PDF; only the text and Markdown exports skip it.

**Repro**

```python
# uv run --with python-pptx python repro.py
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches
prs = Presentation()
s = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])          # Title Only
s.shapes.title.text = "Slide title"
s.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(4), Inches(0.5)).text_frame.text = "Text box body"
t = s.shapes.add_table(2, 2, Inches(0.5), Inches(2.5), Inches(6), Inches(1)).table
for r, row in enumerate([["Cell A1", "Cell B1"], ["Cell A2", "Cell B2"]]):
    for c, v in enumerate(row):
        t.cell(r, c).text = v
prs.save("table.pptx")
```

```sh
deckcraft-cli convert table.pptx table.txt && cat table.txt
deckcraft-cli convert table.pptx table.md  && cat table.md
```

**Expected:** the four cell texts appear (tab-separated rows in `.txt`; a Markdown table in `.md`).

**Actual** (both files):

```
Slide title
	Text box body
```

On five of six template decks we tried, this left out 4–9% of the words (agenda and comparison tables); the sixth has no tables.

<sub>Found while evaluating the CLI for headless use; the repro was reduced and this report drafted with Claude Code.</sub>

title: Brazilian Portuguese (pt_BR) interface translation
author: edurbs
body:
I'd like to add a complete Brazilian Portuguese (pt_BR) interface translation to DeckCraft.

I checked first: there is no pt_BR catalog, issue or PR today. PR #110 ships a generic `pt` catalog whose phrasing leans European Portuguese (`confirmações`, `solicitações de pull`), and PR #34 adds the Ukrainian-only layer. Brazilian Portuguese is a distinct variant (~85% of Portuguese speakers), so I'm proposing it as a separate `pt_BR` language rather than editing the `pt` catalog:

- new `pt_BR.tsv` (1,232 strings, Brazilian vocabulary and Microsoft pt-BR terminology — `commits`/`PRs` kept as loanwords, `rolagem`, `plano de fundo`, `palestrante`, `Ensaiar Intervalos`, curly quotes instead of guillemets);
- `pt` and `pt_BR` distinguished in the language picker (`Português (Portugal)` / `Português (Brasil)`), in the persisted setting (`pt-BR` code) and in system-locale routing (`pt-BR`/`pt_BR` → Brazilian catalog, `pt-PT` and bare `pt` → European).

Same open question as #162: DeckCraft has no i18n layer on `main` yet, and #34 and #110 each add one. My draft PR stacks on #110 (it already carries the `pt` reference catalog and the fuller implementation); it can be retargeted if you prefer #34.

Disclosure: the catalog was produced with AI assistance (GLM, via OpenCode) and follows the repo's TSV format, placeholder and coverage tests; it still needs review by a native speaker before leaving draft — that's me, and feedback from other Brazilian users is welcome.

title: macOS: .pptx / .deckcraft files cannot be opened from Finder (double-click, Open With, drop on Dock icon) — only drag-into-window works
author: infinixmedia2026
body:
Environment
DeckCraft 0.7.0 (build commit d78e657e4cb1e490ceb5445785c052d9cf5ad963), installed via ArtCraft Launcher
macOS 26.7.1 (25G241)
Apple M1 Pro, arm64
App signature: Developer ID, notarized (Gatekeeper: accepted)
Steps to reproduce
In Finder, double-click a .pptx file, or right-click → Open With, or drop the file on the DeckCraft Dock icon.
Same with a .deckcraft file saved by DeckCraft itself.
Expected
DeckCraft opens the presentation.

Actual
The file does not open in DeckCraft.

Dragging the same file into an open DeckCraft window works correctly, so the file itself is fine.

Likely cause (from inspecting the 0.7.0 bundle)
Info.plist has no CFBundleDocumentTypes. It declares UTExportedTypeDeclarations (ai.storyteller.deckcraft.presentation, .deckcraft) and UTImportedTypeDeclarations (org.openxmlformats.presentationml.presentation, .pptx), but never claims a role (Editor/Viewer) for them. So Launch Services does not register DeckCraft as an app that can open these types.
No open-document handler at runtime. The binary is built on winit 0.30.13 / eframe 0.36.2, and contains no application:openURLs: / application:openFiles: implementation on the app delegate. winit 0.30 does not forward macOS open-document events (kAEOpenDocuments) to the app, so even if the plist is fixed, the file path will not reach DeckCraft.
Drag-into-window works because it goes through winit's WindowEvent::DroppedFile, which is a separate path.
Suggested fix
Add CFBundleDocumentTypes entries for ai.storyteller.deckcraft.presentation (Owner, Editor) and org.openxmlformats.presentationml.presentation (Alternate, Editor) with LSItemContentTypes.
Implement application:openURLs: on the NSApplication delegate (e.g. via objc2-app-kit, adding the method to winit's delegate class, or a crate that handles it) and route the paths to the same code that handles DroppedFile. This must also handle files that arrive at launch, before the first window exists.

title: PPTX chart numeric data labels are ignored at series level
author: euisuh
body:
User report: numbers visible on a PowerPoint graph disappear after importing the presentation into DeckCraft. The original user presentation has not been supplied, so this issue describes independently identified source paths and synthetic reproduction coverage rather than claiming to reproduce that exact file.

At DeckCraft `1b64de3`:

- The PPTX reader stores series-level `c:dLbls/c:showVal` in `Series.data_labels`.
- Pie and bar drawing checks chart-wide `Chart.data_labels` instead of the series override. A series that requests labels can therefore render none; an explicitly hidden series can inherit unwanted labels.
- The line/area/scatter/bubble drawing path does not draw numerical data labels.
- A present `<c:showVal/>` has an optional `val` attribute whose default is true; the reader currently treats the missing attribute as unset.

Expected: import group/series visibility without leaking one combo group's settings into another, honour explicit `false`, and render enabled numerical labels for the supported chart paths.

Regression work uses contributor-generated XML/decks and checks the imported model plus actual rendered pixel differences. No proprietary PowerPoint assets or files are added.

Reference for the optional boolean default: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.drawing.charts.showvalue?view=openxml-3.0.1 . This is distinct from resolved rounding issue https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/issues/324 .

Prepared with Codex. Platform-specific comparison against the reporter's original file remains unverified.

### Description

Hi ArtCraft Team,

First of all, I would like to sincerely thank you for all the hard work, time, and dedication you are putting into developing ArtCraft. I have spent a considerable amount of time researching alternatives, including both online tools and desktop applications, but I have not found another solution that offers the same convenient, reliable workflow as PowerPoint for this particular task. title: Bold CJK text drawn in regular weight: East Asian font fallback ignores the run's bold/italic
author: ibakard
body:
**DeckCraft:** 0.7.0 AppImage (`deckcraft-0.7.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage`); the code below is unchanged on `main`
**OS:** Fedora 44, x86_64 (CJK fonts: `google-noto-sans-cjk-vf-fonts`, `google-noto-serif-cjk-vf-fonts`)

## Summary

Bold Chinese, Japanese and Korean text is drawn in regular weight when the run's font has no CJK glyphs, which is the usual case: a text box in Calibri, Aptos or Arial with CJK text. Latin, Cyrillic, Hebrew and Thai text in the same paragraph is bold as expected. The same document in WordCraft 0.7.0 on the same machine draws the CJK text bold.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
# pip install python-pptx
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
prs = Presentation()
s = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
tf = s.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5), Inches(9), Inches(3)).text_frame
for text in ["你好世界 价格", "日本語 ひらがな", "한국어 안녕하세요", "Обща цена", "สวัสดีครับ"]:
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    for bold in (False, True):
        r = p.add_run(); r.text = text + "  "; r.font.name = "Calibri"; r.font.size = Pt(20); r.font.bold = bold
prs.save("cjk-bold.pptx")
```

```sh
deckcraft-cli render cjk-bold.pptx --slide 0 out.png
```

The editing canvas shows the same result, since it draws with `deckcraft_render::render_layout`.

**Expected:** the second copy of each line is bold.
**Actual:** Cyrillic and Thai are bold, but the Chinese, Japanese and Korean copies look the same as the regular ones.

## Cause

`FontDb::cascade` (`crates/fonts/src/fallback.rs`) passes the run's `style` only to the per-script path:

- Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Devanagari have `os_families` entries, so they get `self.face(fam, style)` and the bold face is used.
- CJK scripts have no entry, so they fall through to `self.fallback_for(key, exclude)`, which takes no style. `loaded_fallback_filtered` (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`) sorts candidates by `(f.italic, (f.weight - 400.0).abs())`, so the regular face always wins, even when a bold face of the s…

title: Feature - Live webview element on slide
author: gNovp
body:
When teaching/training, lots of times we need to show external resources like websites/videos during presentations.
Today, the "Link" feature is mostly used (clicking on an image/shape to launch the external webbrowser on the webpage).

It could be great to have an element (like an iframe) that could be placed inside slides, displaying directly live webcontent without leaving DeckCraft.

I know it's not ideal, because it could mean embedding a CEF for instance, but it would be a great feature to have, and a differenciator from PPT.

title: Feature - Copy/Paste/Reference element
author: gNovp
body:
When working on huge PPTs, we sometimes need to have the exact same elements on multiple slides (like a text field with a number, quote, date... or an image for instance).

This can today be easily done with copy/pasting, but the copies are then unlinked (which makes it challenging when that specific content needs to be updated quickly before a presentation). Of course, the Slide Master solves a part of this issue, but it's far from ideal.

What if we had a new entry in the rightclick menu: Paste as Reference.
This button would link the elements together, meaning that an edit on any of these would instantly reflect on all the instanced copies.

This could apply to any element: text fields, images/icons, shapes, media, and could be a huge time saver (especially in huge presentations).
Of course, this feature could be specific to the .deckcraft file format (and copies unlinked if saving as .pptx, as it could be tricky to implement here, even if technically speaking, media in current PPTX files are already instances from ppt/media folder)

title: Feature - Imported objects library
author: gNovp
body:
Following https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/issues/908 , lots of times we need to reference an already imported media (video, image, sound, icon) into an other slide. The way to do so today is to scroll in all the current slides, find the object, copy it, and paste it on the new slide.

It could be great to add a new panel to DeckCraft (PPT has already a library view for icons, pictures, videos etc. Maybe this could be a new tab ?). It would list all the already imported objects (video, images, sounds, icons...) into the current slide deck, ideally presented via thumbnails. Then when clicking on one object of that list, having the option to just add it to the current slide, or add a reference to that object (allowing edits like in https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/issues/908 ) would be a great time saver.

title: Feature - Mark an object as Favorite
author: gNovp
body:
Following https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/issues/909 , a lot of times we have to create object structured in a certain way (like for instance a group containing a square with an icon at the center, and text on the bottom). This kind of structure is then copied/pasted across slides to harmonize the design of a presentation...

But as described in https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/issues/909 , it can be tricky to go back and forward between slides to find this kind of object, and paste it, etc.

Building on the Library feature from https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/issues/909 , it could be great to add to the context menu of selected objects (groups, or single elements like text fields, media etc) a "Favorite" entry. Once clicked, this object would be displayed on top of the the Library panel (from https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/issues/909 ), to allow quick access and integration.

title: Feature request: Add Windows on ARM and Linux on ARM support
author: BraveMomo
body: This is a feature request, not a bug. Please consider adding official support for ARM platforms, specifically Windows on ARM and Linux on ARM.  ARM-based Windows devices are becoming increasingly common, including Windows tablets and lightweight laptops. Linux on ARM is also growing. Supporting these platforms would expand the user base and give the application an advantage in less crowded markets.

title: Feature - Choose the audio device to use per media...
author: gNovp
body:
In more complex presentations (like with a virtual prescripted character for instance, integrated as videos on different slides), it could be great to send the audio to either the default audio device of the system, or choose a different one (like an other speaker).

This is also really usefull when showing a video (let's say with an original audio track in French), and having an audio file playing simultaneously in the slide, sending an English version to another audio device (like wireless earpieces for instance).

A feature like this could be added when a video or audio object is selected, in the "Playback" tab (a "Play audio on: " device list)

title: Feature - Make object scrollable in slide
author: gNovp
body:
Lots of time we have to import content that is not at the right ratio for the current slideshow (for instance vertical infographics, or simply a very long text...).

Of course, Morph transitions can be used to workaround this issue (duplicating the slide, and repositionning the object). But in lots of cases it could be great to just be able to scroll an element (text, image, or even group) in place.

A list control could be added in the "Shape Format" tab, right under the size controls (Height and Width), with 4 choices:

- No scrolling
- Scroll horizontally
- Scroll vertically
- Scroll horizontally and vertically

title: Feature - Advanced slideshow recording options
author: gNovp
body:
PowerPoint allows to record a Slideshow (with timings, microphone and webcam). It's an easy feature integrating the video/audio inside the slide deck, allowing then to export as a video.

But for more professional work, it's lacking.

When the video recording feature will be worked on for DeckCraft, it could be great to ask first to the user the mode of recording:

- Capture and embed (the current mode in Powerpoint, integrating the webcam video as an object in each slide)
- Capture for editing
The latter mode would still record the webcam, audio and timings, but it could place the files after the recording in the same folder as the presentation file itself. Thus, after the recording session, the user would then get: the presentation .deckcraft or .pptx file, a webcam.mp4 file and a slideshow.mp4 file. That would be a huge evolution over what PPT offers (especially in education/training)

And as a bonus, a precut FilmCraft project file embedding these files could also be placed here (or more generally a XML or CSV editlist that could be imported into any Video editing app). This would help tie in the apps in the Craft open ecosystem.

title: [Bug] macOS: Chinese punctuation is entered as ASCII punctuation with multiple input methods
author: Chartreuse310
body:
### Environment
- OS: macOS 26.6.2
- DeckCraft: local source build, run with `cargo run --release -p deckcraft`
- Commit: 1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4
- Input methods: WeChat Input Method and Chatterfly
- Interface language: English

### Description
Chinese punctuation is entered as ASCII punctuation in both slide text and Speaker Notes.

This happens with both WeChat Input Method and Chatterfly, even with English punctuation mode disabled while DeckCraft is focused. The same input methods produce Chinese punctuation correctly in other apps.

Pasting Chinese punctuation into DeckCraft works correctly.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open DeckCraft on macOS.
2. Activate a Chinese input method and ensure English punctuation mode is disabled.
3. Edit a slide text box and type Chinese punctuation, such as `，。`.
4. Repeat in Speaker Notes.

### Expected behavior
The punctuation follows the input method’s Chinese punctuation setting, producing characters such as `，。`.

### Actual behavior
ASCII punctuation such as `,.` is entered instead.

### Additional observations
- Reproduced with two input methods: WeChat Input Method and Chatterfly.
- Affects both slide text and Speaker Notes.
- Other apps work correctly with the same input methods.
- Pasting `你好，世界。` into DeckCraft preserves the Chinese punctuation.
- The local source build includes the macOS CJK font fallback fix from PR #376 (related to #101), which resolved the Chinese missing-glyph boxes in Speaker Notes on my machine. However, this punctuation input issue remains.

### Related issues
- #101 — Korean IME composition and missing-glyph rendering. This report concerns punctuation input; Chinese punctuation renders correctly when pasted.
- #710 — Chinese/Korean input problems on macOS. This report provides a narrower reproduction involving punctuation and two input methods.

These may share an underlying input-handling issue, but I have not confirmed the cause.

title: deckcraft-cli audit: report hidden information in .pptx before sharing
author: ejbarraza
body:
Slide decks routinely carry information the sender doesn't know is there: speaker notes (talking points travel with the file), hidden slides, cropped images that still contain the full uncropped pixels, comments, author names, creator / last-modified-by in core properties, embedded media metadata, OLE embeddings. Cropping a photo in a slide editor doesn't delete the cropped-out region — anyone with the file can recover it.

Proposal: `deckcraft-cli audit <file>` scans the raw OPC package, reports findings as machine-readable JSON with stable finding IDs, and exits nonzero when findings exist (CI-gate usable). v1 finding classes: speaker notes, hidden slides, cropped images retaining full pixel data, comments, author PII (core/app properties), embedded media metadata, OLE embeddings.

Out of scope for v1: sanitizing (strip flagged content with a before/after report; cropped images flagged, not auto-stripped, since that's destructive) — follow-up.

Fixtures will be synthetic, built from ECMA-376 (no PowerPoint-produced files committed, per the clean-room rule).

title: Add musl Linux builds (Alpine Linux, Void musl)
author: vinod2807
body:
### What I'd like

A musl-linked Linux build, so DeckCraft runs on musl distributions — **Alpine Linux** (the most widely used musl distro, and the base of a great many container images) and **Void Linux's musl variant**. None of the currently published Linux artifacts can be used on either.

(The runtime packages a user needs *after* installing such a build are tracked separately in https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/issues/955.)

### Why the current artifacts don't work there

The Linux tarball does contain both binaries:

```
$ tar tzf deckcraft-0.8.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz | grep /bin/
deckcraft-0.8.0-linux-x86_64/bin/deckcraft
deckcraft-0.8.0-linux-x86_64/bin/deckcraft-cli
```

…but both are linked against glibc:

```
$ file .../bin/deckcraft
  ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked,
  interpreter /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, for GNU/Linux 3.2.0, stripped

$ readelf -d .../bin/deckcraft | grep NEEDED
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libasound.so.2]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libgcc_s.so.1]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libm.so.6]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libc.so.6]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [ld-linux-x86-64.so.2]

$ .../bin/deckcraft --version
/bin/ash: .../bin/deckcraft: not found        # Alpine 3.24, i.e. musl
```

`/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2` is glibc's loader; a musl system provides `/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1` instead, so the kernel cannot start the process, and the shell reports that as the very confusing "not found" — which reads like a missing file rather than an ABI mismatch. The same applies to the `.deb`, the `.rpm`, the AppImage (glibc + FUSE) and the Flatpak. `gcompat` is only a partial shim, not a real answer for a GUI application.

### The trap worth avoiding: a static musl build cannot open a window

This is the part that costs a build cycle, so it is worth writing down.

Rust's `*-unknown-linux-musl` targets **link statically by default**. A naive musl build compiles, and `deckcraft-cli` works, but the GUI ne…

title: Document the Linux runtime packages needed after a musl/Alpine install
author: vinod2807
body:
Split out of #954 in response to triage, which asked for these to be tracked separately. This ticket is **only the documentation side**; the build side (actually producing a musl artifact) stays in #954.

### Why this is worth writing down

A DeckCraft GUI loads its windowing and GPU dependencies with `dlopen`. In the current release those names appear in the binary as **strings with no matching `DT_NEEDED` entry**:

```
libX11.so.6      libXcursor.so.1      libvulkan.so.1      libwayland-client.so.0
```

Only `libasound.so.2` is a hard link-time dependency. The practical problem: when a `dlopen` target is missing, the app does not fail with a clear "requires libX" message, and a package manager cannot know about it either. It fails only at startup, so the user has no way to tell what to install. That is exactly the class of thing install instructions exist for.

### What the instructions should cover

For Alpine Linux — and Void's musl variant, which uses the same `/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1` loader:

```sh
apk add libxkbcommon libx11 libxcursor libxrandr libxi \
        wayland-libs-client \
        alsa-lib \
        vulkan-loader mesa-vulkan-swrast \
        fontconfig freetype ttf-dejavu
```

Optional, depending on what the user needs:

```sh
apk add mesa-gl mesa-egl mesa-dri-gallium   # OpenGL fallback if Vulkan is unavailable
apk add cups-client cups-libs               # printing
apk add xdg-desktop-portal                  # native file dialogs
```

Points worth spelling out:

- `alsa-lib` is DeckCraft-specific rather than generic: `deckcraft` has a hard `DT_NEEDED` on `libasound.so.2` because presentations play audio and video. The CLI does not need it.
- `mesa-vulkan-swrast` is the software Vulkan driver and works on any machine, including VMs. Users with a real GPU should install their vendor driver instead (`mesa-vulkan-intel`, `mesa-vulkan-ati`, `mesa-vulkan-nouveau`, ...).
- On older integrated GPUs with no Vulkan support the app falls back to CPU renderi…

title: Web build: let the host page supply fonts through a manifest, like PhotoCraft does
author: Tof33
body:
### Summary

On the web build, DeckCraft can only use the faces compiled into the wasm. There is no way for the page that hosts it to offer additional fonts, so a deck that relies on a brand or corporate typeface is drawn with a substitute, and a `.pptx` opened in the browser loses its intended look.

PhotoCraft already solves exactly this, and the mechanism is small. This issue asks for the same thing in DeckCraft.

### Why it matters more here than elsewhere

A presentation is a document people hand to someone else. The typeface is part of what makes it look right, and a substitution is visible on every slide — more so than in an image editor, where a missing face usually affects one text layer.

Organisations that host the web build generally have one or two mandated typefaces. Today the only way to get them in is to rebuild DeckCraft, which means leaving the published release behind and redoing the work at every version.

### What the code says

`crates/ui-egui/src/uifonts.rs`, still the case at `v0.8.0`:

> Nothing is bundled for it: on the web, where there are no installed fonts, only the embedded faces are used.

That is about script fallback, but it is the same constraint: the web build has no font source other than itself.

I checked the wasm we serve (`deckcraft-web-3d451cd28e31e9b6_bg.wasm`, ~25 MB uncompressed): `Inter` appears 94 times, while the two typefaces I would want to add appear zero times. Nothing to toggle — the faces simply are not there.

### What PhotoCraft does

PhotoCraft reads a `fonts/manifest.txt` next to the page, documented in its `HOSTING.md` under *Fonts*. One line per face:

```
Family | Style | path/to/file.otf
```

Only the first three fields are read; the path is relative to the page. Two details worth keeping if this is ported:

- the family must be the one the font **declares** (`name` table, id 16 when present, else id 1) rather than the name one would like to see in the menu — PhotoCraft warns in the console and keeps its o…
