Objects (texts, groups, etc) marked as Favorites can also be featured at the top of this new tab (mentioned in #910 ).

title: 0.8.0 web build panics at startup: "no pids on this platform"
author: Tof33
body:
### Summary

The `deckcraft-web-0.8.0.zip` package panics while starting up and never
shows the app. `v0.7.0`, served the same way from the same host, starts
normally — so this is a regression in 0.8.0.

### What happens

Console, in order:

```
[info]  deckcraft-web 0.8.0: wgpu backend BrowserWebGpu
[error] panicked at library/std/src/sys/process/unsupported.rs:335:5:
        no pids on this platform
[error] Uncaught RuntimeError: unreachable
```

The wasm loads fine (10.4 MB transferred, 85 ms) and the build identifies
itself, so this is not a packaging or transport problem — something on the
startup path calls into `std::process` (a pid lookup), which is `unsupported`
on `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and panics.

### Side-by-side, same host, same page

| | 0.7.0 | 0.8.0 |
|---|---|---|
| wasm loaded | yes | yes |
| version line in console | `deckcraft-web 0.7.0` | `deckcraft-web 0.8.0` |
| `event handlers installed.` | yes | never reached |
| `<canvas>` size | 2108×1622 | 300×150 (untouched default) |
| panic | — | `no pids on this platform` |

The canvas size is the clearest tell: 300×150 is the HTML default, so the app
never got as far as sizing its own surface.

### Reproduction

1. Serve `deckcraft-web-0.8.0/` as a static directory (any host; I use a
   plain static file server, wasm served with `application/wasm`).
2. Open `index.html`.
3. The page stays blank; the console shows the panic above.

Chromium 141, macOS 15.5, WebGPU available (0.7.0 uses it on the same
machine).

### Note

`guard.rs:29` logs the panic as `ERROR: [deckcraft_engine::guard] panic at …`
just before it propagates, so the guard sees it — that may be a good place to
start looking for who asks for a pid.

Happy to test a build.

title: Presenter View: investigate sluggishness and keyboard control behavior
author: earlvanze
body:
## Report

A Linux user reports that Presenter View is buggy and slow during a presentation. They also requested direct presenter controls:

- Left and Right arrow keys to move between slides.
- Up and Down arrow keys to scroll speaker notes.
- `P` to play or pause video.
- A red glowing pointer.

## Current coverage

The slide-show key handler already maps Left and Right arrows to previous and next slides. Presenter View itself renders the current slide, a next-slide preview, notes, timer, and previous/next buttons. The window renders its next-slide preview synchronously when it changes, which may contribute to sluggishness on complex decks.

Video pause behavior is separately tracked in #362, and slide-show ink/laser work is in open PR #161. This issue focuses on measuring and fixing Presenter View responsiveness, then ensuring its keyboard controls work independently of the show window.

## Reproduction information needed

- DeckCraft version/build and Linux desktop session.
- Display count, resolution, and GPU/driver.
- Deck size, media, animations, and approximate notes length.
- Whether slowdown occurs at launch, when advancing slides, while scrolling notes, or continuously.
- A small reproducible deck or screen recording if possible.

## Acceptance criteria

- Profile Presenter View with complex slides, media, and long notes, and remove identified stalls.
- Presenter-window left/right navigation works reliably without focus ambiguity.
- Up/down scroll the notes pane while it has focus.
- Clarify and implement a conflict-free media play/pause shortcut where applicable.
- Keep the current slide show responsive while Presenter View updates.

title: [Bug] Saving a .pptx with a modern comment writes malformed XML (undeclared a: prefix); PowerPoint refuses the file
author: erwanpaccard
body:
**What happens.** When a deck contains a modern comment, deckcraft writes `ppt/comments/modernComment*.xml` with a root that declares only `xmlns:p188`, but the body uses `a:bodyPr`, `a:p`, `a:r`, `a:t`. The `a:` prefix is unbound, so the part is not well-formed XML and PowerPoint refuses the saved file as damaged (0x80070570). Silent failure: exit 0, no warning, file unusable in PowerPoint.

**Repro 1 (no input file needed).**
```
deckcraft-cli run --sample --cmd comment.add='{"text":"hello"}' --save c1.pptx
python -c "import zipfile,xml.dom.minidom as m; z=zipfile.ZipFile('c1.pptx'); [m.parseString(z.read(n)) for n in z.namelist() if 'modernComment' in n]"
```
raises `unbound prefix`. Opening `c1.pptx` in PowerPoint (COM `Presentations.Open`) is refused.

**Repro 2 (round trip).** Create a one-slide deck in PowerPoint with one comment, then `deckcraft-cli run --in in.pptx --save out.pptx`. The input parses and opens fine. In the input, `p188:cmLst` declares `xmlns:a` and `xmlns:r`; in `out.pptx` only `xmlns:p188` is left, and `out.pptx` is refused. Same on a real 87-slide deck with 2 modern comments.

**Where.** `crates/pptx/src/write/mod.rs`, `modern_comments_xml` (root `p188:cmLst` lacks `xmlns:a`; `tx_body` uses `a:`). Introduced by 69d4893 (PR #280, #70), shipped in 0.8.0. 0.7.0 is not affected (it only wrote the legacy `comment1.xml`). Same on `main` (22db926). Same class as #412, but for comments. The sibling `p188:authorLst` only uses `p188:`; I did not audit other writers.

**Suggested fix.** Declare `xmlns:a` (`NS_A`) on `p188:cmLst`. Adding it by hand to the saved file makes it open in PowerPoint (checked on the 87-slide deck). A regression test could save a deck with a comment and parse each written part with a namespace-aware XML parser; the existing tests in `tests/comments.rs` only use `contains`.

**Environment.** deckcraft-cli 0.8.0, Windows 11 x64 portable.

title: CLI render blocks on macOS while the font scan waits on an app-data privacy prompt (Office CloudFonts folder, 0.8.0)
author: rex4539
body:
## What happens

`deckcraft-cli render` 0.8.0 can block indefinitely during start-up on macOS when Microsoft Office is installed. It stays blocked until someone answers a macOS privacy prompt asking to access data from other apps. The prompt is triggered by the font scan, not by anything in the deck. It was observed with a one-slide deck holding a single column chart, made with python-pptx, which uses no Office cloud fonts. With 0.5.0, a similar deck rendered in about 0.2 s.

## Cause

`system_font_dirs()` in `crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs` (v0.8.0) adds:

```
~/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts
```

On macOS 14 and later, a process that reads another app's container is subject to App Data protection. If the responsible app has not been granted access, macOS shows the "would like to access data from other apps" prompt, and the `opendir` call blocks until it is answered. `scan_font_dirs` runs on the main thread before the first lookup, so the whole render waits.

Sampled while blocked (0 % CPU):

```
FontDb::face
  FontDb::try_family
    FontDb::load_cataloged
      FontDb::load_family
        OnceLock::initialize (ensure_catalog)
          FontDb::scan_font_dirs
            std::sys::fs::read_dir
              __opendir2 -> open$NOCANCEL -> __open_nocancel
```

A plain `timeout 10 /bin/ls` of the same folder also timed out, with rc 124, while the prompt was pending. That shows the block comes from the OS, not from deckcraft code. Once the prompt was answered, the same commands returned immediately.

## Repro

You need macOS 14 or later, Microsoft Office installed so that `~/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office` exists, and a terminal or host app that has not yet been granted access to other apps' data.

```zsh
d=$(mktemp -d)
timeout 20 deckcraft-cli render --sample "$d/a.png"; echo "rc=$?"
mkdir -p "$d/home/Library" && ln -s "$HOME/Library/Fonts" "$d/home/Library/Fonts"
HOME="$d/home" timeout 20 deckcraft-cli render --sample "$d/b.…

title: Feat: Add support for VBA macros and scripting (.pptm format)
author: nestorvashenko
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Yes. Currently, DeckCraft focuses on static slides and lacks support for embedded macros or scripting runtimes. Many enterprise users and educators rely heavily on PowerPoint presentations with embedded VBA macros (`.pptm` format) for advanced slide animations, dynamic quiz/trivia interactions, or custom automated deck rendering. 

Without VBA or macro preservation, importing legacy interactive presentations completely breaks their core functionality.

### Describe the solution you'd like
I would like to see VBA/macro/scripting compatibility introduced into DeckCraft:
1. **Preservation & Round-trip:** Ensure that opening and saving `.pptm` or macro-enabled `.pptx` presentations does not strip out or destroy the embedded VBA macro binary files.
2. **Execution / Interaction Runtime:** A basic runtime layer to support slide-trigger events controlled by macros (e.g., executing code when a specific shape/button is clicked during a presentation).

### Describe alternatives you've considered
* Manually rewriting dynamic animations and triggers for every single deck, which is highly inefficient for large catalogs of legacy interactive training materials.
* Keeping MS PowerPoint just to run interactive presentations, which defeats the purpose of fully migrating to the open-source ArtCraft ecosystem.

### Additional context
As DeckCraft gains popularity as a lightweight and high-performance presentation tool, adding macro support will close a major gap for power users who build advanced interactive and automated slide decks.

title: Show: hold the left mouse button for the laser pointer
author: Zdaymen
body:
## Summary

During a slide show, pressing and holding the left mouse button should show the laser dot for as long as the button is held. Releasing it hides the dot and leaves the slide where it was. PowerPoint does this, and presenters coming from PowerPoint reach for it out of habit.

## Today

- Merged in #441: Cmd/Ctrl+L or the on-screen button toggles the laser.
- Open in #636: holding Ctrl shows the dot while the key is held.

Both need the keyboard, or a trip to the on-screen button. That's awkward when the presenter is standing away from the laptop with a mouse or clicker, or just wants to point for a second.

## Proposed behavior

1. In a show, a left-button press held past a short threshold (about 250–300 ms) shows the laser dot in the show's laser colour (from Set Up Slide Show, per #636).
2. The dot follows the pointer while the button stays down and leaves no ink, like the current laser.
3. Releasing after the threshold hides the dot and **does not advance** the slide or trigger the next build.
4. A quick click (released before the threshold) advances exactly as it does today.
5. If the pen or highlighter is active, the press keeps drawing as it does now. The hold gesture applies only in arrow/default mode.

## Nice to have

- A setting to turn the gesture off for people who prefer instant click-to-advance.
- Long-press on touch and pen input does the same thing.
- The dot shows in the presenter window and on the audience display (see #646).
- Record Slide Show keeps a laser trace while the button is held, as it does for Ctrl in #636.

## Test plan idea

- Start a show, press and hold the left button, and move: the dot follows. Release: the dot disappears and the slide hasn't changed.
- A quick click still advances.
- With the pen active, press and hold draws ink and shows no laser.

title: Product Requirements Document: Real-Time Collaboration & Multi-User Sharing (Artcraft)
author: MichalJankura
body:
# Product Requirements Document: Real-Time Collaboration & Multi-User Sharing (Artcraft)

## 1. Overview & Objectives

The goal is to extend the Artcraft presentation platform with real-time multi-user co-authoring capabilities (similar to Google Slides or Figma). The module must deliver seamless state synchronization, real-time presence indicators, and flexible role-based access control.

---

## 2. Functional Requirements

### 2.1 Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

* **Owner:** Full administrative control over the presentation, including permission management, ownership transfer, and deletion.
* **Editor:** Can edit canvas elements, layouts, text, and media, as well as leave comments in real time.
* **Commenter:** Read-only access to presentation content with the ability to add and reply to comment threads.
* **Viewer:** Read-only access, including the ability to run the presentation in Presenter Mode.

### 2.2 Sharing Engine & Access Control

* **Email Invitations:** Invite specific users with predefined access roles.
* **Link Sharing Options:**
* Private Link (restricted to invited users).
* Public Link (configurable permissions: Viewer / Commenter / Editor).
* Password protection and link expiration dates (for premium accounts).


* **Domain/Organization Sharing:** Workspace-wide access control (e.g., all users with an `@company.com` email address).

### 2.3 Real-Time Presence & Co-Editing

* **Live Cursors:** Display live mouse pointers of active collaborators with user avatars/names and unique color indicators.
* **Slide Activity Indicators:** Thumbnail panel badges showing which user is currently viewing or editing specific slides.
* **Object-Level Locking:** Non-blocking temporary lock on individual elements (text boxes, shapes, images) while actively being modified by a user to prevent edit conflicts.
* **Contextual Commenting:** Pin comments directly to specific canvas objects with support for `@mentions` and thread status management (e.g., *Resolve*).

title: chart.data drops the chart's number format, label/legend font sizes and auto-title
author: chico1506
body:
**Version:** deckcraft-cli 0.8.0 (release build, macOS universal), macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon. Checked against PowerPoint for Mac 16.111.

## What happens

`chart.data` on an existing chart rebuilds the chart XML from the model and drops formatting that the user didn't ask to change:

- the series and data-label number format (`0.0"%"` becomes `General`, so `50.5%` is shown as `50.5`)
- the font sizes of the data labels (16 pt) and legend (18 pt), so PowerPoint falls back to its defaults
- the automatic title: before the edit the chart had no `c:title` and showed the series name. After the edit an explicit title holding the *old* series name (`Q1`) is written, even though the series is now `Q2`

Exit code 0, no warning. DeckCraft's own render of the edited file still looks like the original, so an agent that checks its work with `deckcraft-cli render` can't see the loss. Only PowerPoint shows it.

A plain open → save (`deckcraft-cli convert`) keeps all of this. Only `chart.data` loses it.

## Repro

```python
# make.py: python-pptx 1.0.2
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE, XL_LEGEND_POSITION
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt

prs = Presentation()
s = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
d = CategoryChartData(number_format='0.0"%"')
d.categories = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma"]
d.add_series("Q1", (50.5, 30.2, 19.3))
ch = s.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.DOUGHNUT, Inches(1), Inches(1), Inches(8), Inches(5), d).chart
ch.has_legend = True
ch.legend.position = XL_LEGEND_POSITION.RIGHT
ch.legend.font.size = Pt(18)
pl = ch.plots[0]
pl.has_data_labels = True
pl.data_labels.show_value = True
pl.data_labels.number_format = '0.0"%"'
pl.data_labels.number_format_is_linked = False
pl.data_labels.font.size = Pt(16)
prs.save("chart-formatted.pptx")
```

```sh
deckcraft-cli run --in chart-formatted.pptx \
  --cmd 'chart.data={"id":2,"series":[{"name":"Q2","values":[48.1,31.0,20.9]}]}' \

**Version:** deckcraft-cli 0.8.0 (release build, macOS universal), macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon.

## What happens

A chart that DeckCraft creates (`insert.chart`) or edits (`chart.data`) is saved to .pptx without an embedded workbook. There is no `ppt/embeddings/*.xlsx`, no chart relationship to one, and no `c:externalData`. The chart is drawn correctly, but PowerPoint's **Edit Data** has no workbook to open, so whoever receives the deck can't change the numbers from PowerPoint.

#335 fixed this for *unchanged* charts (0.8.0 keeps them byte for byte, thank you). The remaining case is any chart DeckCraft writes itself. `file-format-parity.md` describes dropping the workbook on edit as deliberate ("rather than writing a stale one"). This issue asks for a fresh workbook instead of none.

## Repro

```sh
deckcraft-cli run --sample \
  --cmd 'slide.new={"layout":"blank"}' \
  --cmd 'insert.chart={"type":"column","categories":["A","B"],"series":[{"name":"S","values":[1,2]}]}' \
  --save new-chart.pptx
unzip -Z1 new-chart.pptx | grep -E 'charts|embeddings'
# ppt/charts/chart1.xml
# ppt/charts/chart2.xml          <- no ppt/embeddings/, no ppt/charts/_rels/
```

Editing an existing chart that has a workbook gives the same result:

```sh
# chart.pptx = any deck with a native chart saved by PowerPoint (has ppt/embeddings/Microsoft_Excel_Worksheet.xlsx)
deckcraft-cli convert chart.pptx kept.pptx           # workbook kept (fixed by #335)
deckcraft-cli run --in chart.pptx --cmd 'chart.data={"id":<chart id>,"series":[{"name":"S","values":[1,2,3]}]}' --save edited.pptx
unzip -Z1 edited.pptx | grep -c embeddings            # 0
```

## Expected

When DeckCraft writes a chart from its model, it also writes a small workbook built from the same categories and series, with a relationship and `c:externalData`, like PowerPoint and python-pptx do. The workbook then matches the chart's cache, so it is never stale, and Edit Data works in PowerPoint.

Why it matters: the main use of the CLI/MCP…

title: Web build: report the open document in the viewport title
author: robertcsakany
body:
The web build sends no `ViewportCommand::Title` naming the open document (eframe would log it as `Unhandled egui viewport command: Title(…)` on the web). WordCraft, GridCraft, PhotoCraft and VectorCraft do (`<document>[ •] — <App>`).

An embedding host (pi-agent-dashboard runs the web build in a sandboxed iframe and delivers the document as a synthetic drop) uses that title to confirm WHICH document the app opened and whether it has unsaved changes. Without it the host can only assume the drop worked after a delay; when a drop is refused, the app's default document is mistaken for the file (seen with CADCraft 0.8.0 and a `.dwg`: it showed `Drawing1`).

Ask: send `Title("<file name>[ •] — <App>")` on open, rename and dirty change, like WordCraft.

author: sf-987
body:
It's common to group together multiple objects (such as drawn boxes) and then manipulate them at once.

For example, draw two different rectangles on the screen, then group them.  Now use Format Object -> Fill -> (any different color) or -> Line Color (any different color).  Nothing happens. The MSFT office program this is attempting to reach parity with allows these changes to be done as a group.  It would be nice to see these added.

title: Shape Fill / Line does not retain last selection
author: sf-987
body:
In MSFT office, the shape fill or line style (and other functions) do not retain their last setting.

If you have many objects on the screen, in MSFT office you can choose one object, set the fill color and line color, and then the most recent choice is remembered.  You can then select a given object and just click on the "fill color" or "line style" label, and it sets the object accordingly.

In DeckCraft, you have to click the down arrow to get the list of colors, and manually scroll over to the color you want each and every time.

It would be nice to match the feature in MSFT office to make it faster to work on complex materials.

title: `run`: accept commands from a file or stdin (Windows command line limit)
author: erwanpaccard
body:
**Summary.** `deckcraft-cli run` takes every command as a `--cmd` argument. On Windows the command line is capped at about 32,767 characters (`CreateProcess`), so a script of a few hundred to a thousand commands cannot be run in one call, and there is no way to give `run` the commands in a file or on stdin. The MCP server (`batch`) has no such limit and works for us, but a CLI-only option would be simpler for scripts that do not want to host an MCP client.

**Environment.** deckcraft-cli 0.8.0 (windows-x64-portable), Windows 11 x64. I also read `apps/deckcraft-cli/src/main.rs` on `main` (a31b990, 2026-10-20): `run` still only parses `--in`, `--sample`, `--cmd`, `--save`, `--export`, `--export-params`, `--print`.

**Steps.** Save as `repro.py`, run `python repro.py path\to\deckcraft-cli.exe`:
```python
import subprocess, sys, json
exe = sys.argv[1]
cmds = ['slide.new=' + json.dumps({"title": f"Slide {i}"}) for i in range(1200)]
args = [exe, "run"] + [a for c in cmds for a in ("--cmd", c)] + ["--save", "big.deckcraft"]
print("command line length:", sum(len(a) + 1 for a in args))
try:
    r = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True)
    print("exit", r.returncode, r.stderr[:200])
except OSError as e:
    print("OSError:", e)
```

**Actual.** `command line length: 47026`, then `OSError: [WinError 206]` (file name or extension too long). Nothing is saved. Real example from a deck generator: a 3-slide deck of 942 commands is 55,545 characters, well over the limit (an 11-slide mixed deck of 198 commands is 9,361 characters and fits).
Other ways I tried to pass commands, all refused:
- `--cmd @file` and `--cmd -`: ``unknown command `@file` `` / ``unknown command `-` `` (the value is read as a command id);
- `--cmd-file`, `--script`, `--batch`, `--commands` and `run @file`: ``unknown option``.

**Expected.** `run --cmd-file FILE`: one command per line, parsed like a `--cmd` value (`id={json}`, or an id alone when it takes no parameters). Suggested details:
- file…

title: Animation Pane: expand a by-paragraph build into one row per paragraph (own start, timing, order)
author: pawel-gla
body:
A by-paragraph text build (Effect Options › Sequence › By Paragraph) works, but it shows as a single row in the Animation Pane, and every paragraph gets the same start, duration and delay. There is no way to handle one bullet on its own.

In PowerPoint the pane can expand such a build ("Expand contents" chevron, or a click on the arrow under the row) into one row per paragraph. Each row can then:
- have its own start (On Click / With Previous / After Previous), duration and delay
- be reordered among the slide's other effects
- be collapsed back into the group row

The typical use: a list of bullets in one text box, where bullet 2 appears **With Previous** alongside a picture, bullet 3 together with a chart, and so on. Splitting the list into separate text boxes is the usual workaround, but then line spacing, numbering and alignment have to be kept in sync by hand.

Wanted:
1. Animation Pane: an expand/collapse control on by-paragraph builds, showing one row per paragraph, each editable and draggable like any other effect (including on the advanced timeline).
2. Optionally: with the caret in, or a selection inside, a paragraph of a text box, Add Animation applies to that paragraph only.

The model seems to support this already: `Animation.paragraph` (`crates/model/src/anim.rs`) targets one paragraph, and the timeline currently shows the first paragraph of a build as its bar (`crates/ui-egui/src/animtimeline.rs`). What's missing is the UI to create and edit those per-paragraph effects.

title: Presenter mode: bullet markers of rich-text lists in speaker notes are missing
author: marcfischer
body:
## Description

Speaker notes containing a rich-text bullet list (imported from an existing presentation) are rendered correctly in the notes view. When switching to presenter mode, the bullet markers are missing, so the items are shown as plain lines and the list structure is lost.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an existing presentation whose speaker notes contain a rich-text bullet list.
2. Check the notes view: the list is rendered with bullets.
3. Switch to presenter mode.

## Expected behavior

The notes in presenter mode show the same bullet list as in the notes view.

## Actual behavior

In presenter mode the bullet markers are missing. The items appear without bullets.

## Additional notes

Other rich-text formatting in the notes may be affected as well (numbered lists, nested lists, indentation, bold/italic, links). I haven't checked this systematically yet.

Possible cause: the presenter view might use a different renderer or a style reset (e.g. `list-style: none`) that drops list markers.

## Environment

- DeckCraft version: 0.9.0
- Source presentation format: pptx

title: [Feature Request] [DeckCraft] insert_chart accepts x, y, w, h
author: forhadkhan
body:
## Environment
- DeckCraft 0.9.0 (`deckcraft-cli --version`), Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, .deb from ArtCraft Launcher 0.6.1
- Driven by an MCP client over stdio: `deckcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root <dir> --automation-write-root <dir>`

## Steps
1. `new_presentation` `{}`, then `add_slide` `{"layout":"titleOnly","title":"Numbers"}`
2. `insert_chart` `{"type":"column","title":"Sales","categories":["A","B","C"],"series":[{"name":"S","values":[1,2,3]}]}`
3. `inspect_slide` `{}`

## Actual
The chart box is always `[144.0, 81.0, 672.0, 378.0]` (x, y, w, h in points). `insert_chart` has no position or size arguments. `add_shape`, `add_text_box`, `insert_picture` and `insert_table` all take a box.

## Expected / request
Optional `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` on `insert_chart`, the same as the other insert tools, so a chart can share a slide with other content without a second command to move and resize it.

Related: #1046 (chart data options).

title: [Feature Request] [DeckCraft] Accept more than one --automation-read-root / --automation-write-root
author: forhadkhan
body:
## Environment
- DeckCraft 0.9.0 (`deckcraft-cli --version`), Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, .deb from ArtCraft Launcher 0.6.1
- Driven by an MCP client over stdio

## Steps
```
deckcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /tmp --automation-read-root /var
deckcraft-cli mcp --automation-write-root /tmp --automation-write-root /var
```

## Actual
Both exit at once with:
```
deckcraft-cli: --automation-read-root given twice
```
(and the same for `--automation-write-root`).

## Expected / request
Allow each option more than once (or a list of folders), so one MCP session can read from a project folder and a shared assets folder, or write to an output folder and a scratch folder, without widening the root to their common parent. The confinement stays as strict as today: only the listed folders are allowed.

Other Craft apps (PhotoCraft, EffectCraft, FigCraft) already accept the option twice.

title: [Audit] Unbounded audio decode, on the UI thread for duration probing
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-01 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** High  
**Category:** DoS / unbounded allocation  
**Confidence:** Confirmed by code trace, figures estimated  
**Audit ID:** F-01

> Previously reported as #399, which was closed without a fix (PR #498 was not merged). The code at the audited commit still accumulates PCM with no budget.

**Evidence.**

The decode loop has no ceiling on `out`:

[`crates/media/src/audio.rs:180-230`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/media/src/audio.rs#L180-L230)
```rust
let mut out: Vec<f32> = Vec::new();
...
loop {
    let packet = match format.next_packet() { ... };
    ...
    if let Some(b) = buf.as_mut() {
        b.copy_interleaved_ref(decoded);
        out.extend_from_slice(b.samples());
    }
```

`probe` decodes the whole file to learn its length when the header has none:

[`crates/media/src/probe.rs:76-80`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/media/src/probe.rs#L76-L80)

    if let Ok(pcm) = crate::audio::decode(bytes) {
```

`probe` runs on the UI thread from `MediaCache::duration_of`:

[`crates/ui-egui/src/media.rs:130,194`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/ui-egui/src/media.rs#L130)

```

title: [Audit] Video decoders allow unbounded allocation per sample
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-02 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** High  
**Category:** DoS / unbounded allocation  
**Confidence:** Confirmed by code reading (not executed)  
**Audit ID:** F-02

Three related defects. Each ends in an allocation abort. Each is reachable when the victim plays an embedded video, and on `insert.video`, whose `poster_png` decodes the first sample synchronously ([`engine/src/cmd/insert.rs:1289`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs#L1289)).

**(a) Pictures per sample are unbounded, and each is converted to full-size RGBA.**

- In [`media/src/video.rs:74,141,236`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/media/src/video.rs#L74), every `Codec::decode` does `…into_iter().map(convert).collect()`, and [`video.rs:426-430`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/media/src/video.rs#L426-L430) extends an unbounded `ready: VecDeque`.
- AV1 pushes an output for every `show_existing_frame` header ([`av1/src/decoder.rs:463`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/av1/src/decoder.rs#L463)):
  ```rust
  let shown = self.frame_header(&mut r, temporal_id, spatial_id)?;
  if let Some(o) = shown { out.push((o, tu, spatial_id)); continue; }
  ```
  A few bytes per repeated frame header yields a full YUV copy plus about 8 MB of RGBA at 1080p.
- H.264 (`decoder.rs:250-279,379`) and HEVC (`decoder.rs:191-218,321-324`) likewise start a new picture for every slice with `first_mb_in_slice == 0` / `first_slice_segment_in_pic_flag`.

**(b) HEVC fabricates missing references without a budget.**

[`hevc/src/decoder.rs:443-448`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd…

title: [Audit] PPTX tags part is re-parsed and copied per reference
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-03 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** High  
**Category:** DoS / amplification  
**Confidence:** Confirmed by code reading, memory figure estimated  
**Audit ID:** F-03

**Evidence.** [`crates/pptx/src/read/mod.rs:193-205`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/pptx/src/read/mod.rs#L193-L205), called for every shape (`read/shapes.rs:169`) and every slide (`mod.rs:1100`):

```rust
for t in list.children_named("tags").take(100) {
    let Some(doc) = t.attr("r:id").and_then(|id| part.rels.get(id)).and_then(|r| imp.pkg.xml(&r.target)) else { continue };
    for tag in doc.root.children_named("tag").take(10_000) {
        if let Some(name) = tag.attr("name") {
            out.push((name.to_string(), tag.attr("val").unwrap_or("").to_string()));
```

`Package::xml` ([`opc.rs:112-125`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/pptx/src/opc.rs#L112-L125)) parses afresh on every call, with no cache. The only caps are per part (96 MiB) and per element count. Nothing bounds the total copied into the model.

**Scenario.**

1. A tags part of about 96 MiB of `val` text deflates to about 100 KB.
2. One shape lists `<p:tags r:id="rId1"/>` 100 times. That is 100 parses of 96 MiB and about 9.6 GB of `String` for a single shape.
3. With 20,000 shapes (`MAX_SHAPES`) this is unbounded in practice.
4. The parse runs on the `deckcraft-open` thread ([`ui-egui/src/opening.rs:42`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/ui-egui/src/opening.rs#L42)). A panic there is reported, but OOM aborts the process.
5. The same applies to the MCP server and `deckcraft-cli` batch runs.

**Fix sketch.**
```diff
+// Imp: cache parsed tag lists by part, and share them (Arc<[(String,String)]>)
+pub tags_…

title: [Audit] Unbounded device-space geometry reaches vello's flattener
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-05 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** High (abort)  
**Category:** DoS / unbounded allocation  
**Confidence:** Plausible (traced into vello source, not executed)  
**Audit ID:** F-05

**Evidence.**

- Shape sizes are clamped only from below: [`pptx/src/read/dml.rs:298-305`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/pptx/src/read/dml.rs#L298-L305). `El::i64` clamps to ±9e18 EMU.
- Custom geometry guides are clamped to ±1e15 ([`pptx/src/custgeom.rs:31-33`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/pptx/src/custgeom.rs#L31-L33)) and then scaled by `w / pw` ([`render/src/lib.rs:526-531`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/render/src/lib.rs#L526-L531)).
- Group child scale `group.w / ch.width()` is unbounded ([`geom/src/lib.rs:162-166`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/geom/src/lib.rs#L162-L166)), compounding across up to 32 nesting levels ([`render/src/lib.rs:846`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/render/src/lib.rs#L846)).

title: [Audit] Media probe and video `open` run on the UI thread without a panic guard
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-06 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Medium  
**Category:** Panic on unguarded path  
**Confidence:** Confirmed (path) / Plausible (concrete panic)  
**Audit ID:** F-06

**Evidence.**

- [`ui-egui/src/media.rs:130`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/ui-egui/src/media.rs#L130) calls `deckcraft_media::probe` and `media.rs:203` calls `VideoFeed::new`. Both run on the egui update thread.
- [`probe.rs:54-58`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/media/src/probe.rs#L54-L58) calls `probe_mp4` / `probe_mkv` / `probe_asf` with **no `catch_unwind`**. Only the symphonia branch is wrapped.
- [`feed.rs:38`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/media/src/feed.rs#L38) calls `VideoDecoder::open`, which parses the container and runs `configure_avcc` / `configure_hvcc` on the UI thread.
- `configure_avcc` / `configure_hvcc` dispatch **any** NAL type in the config record, slices included, to the full decode pipeline ([`h264/decoder.rs:216-239,311-338`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/h264/src/decoder.rs#L216-L239), [`hevc/decoder.rs:160-180,287`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/hevc/src/decoder.rs#L160-L180)). That makes #1163(b) reachable on the UI thread, and lets `dispatch` block it while `in_flight` is full.
- Clippy reports 89 / 52 / 42 non-test indexing sites in isobmff / matroska / ogg, plus 32 in media.
- A panic in `eframe::App::update` unwinds out of the event loop and ends the process.

**Impact.** Any reachable panic in these demuxers or config paths crashes the whole app when a slide's media is played. In debug builds, the H.264/HEVC P…

title: [Audit] MP4 constant-size sample tables amplify metadata
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-07 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Medium  
**Category:** DoS / amplification  
**Confidence:** Confirmed (code), Plausible (abort depends on RAM)  
**Audit ID:** F-07

**Evidence.** [`isobmff/src/demux.rs:600-611`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/isobmff/src/demux.rs#L600-L611):
```rust
} else {
    // Samples of constant size must fit in the file: clamp absurd counts.
    sample_count = (n as u64).min(file_len / const_size as u64) as usize;
}
```

Then `demux.rs:742-745`:
```rust
if sample_count > MAX_SAMPLES { return Err(...) }   // MAX_SAMPLES = 1 << 26
samples.reserve(sample_count);
```

- With `const_size = 1`, `sample_count` can equal the file length, up to 67M.
- A `Sample` is about 40 bytes, so a ~64 MiB run of zeros (near-free inside a deflated `.pptx`) yields about 2.7 GB of `Vec<Sample>`.
- `mp4guard::tables_fit` protects only the symphonia path, not this demuxer.
- Reached from probe (UI thread), `VideoFeed::new` and the poster.

**Fix sketch.** Clamp by a realistic minimum sample size (for example, `file_len / max(const_size, 16)`). Lower `MAX_SAMPLES` for in-memory media (for example, 2^22). Or store compact runs for constant-size tracks instead of materialising every `Sample`.

title: [Audit] Quadratic `more_rbsp_data` in H.264 CAVLC
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-08 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Medium (hang)  
**Category:** DoS / CPU  
**Confidence:** Confirmed  
**Audit ID:** F-08

**Evidence.** [`bitstream/src/lib.rs:162-179`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/bitstream/src/lib.rs#L162-L179) scans backwards from the end of the RBSP on every call:

```rust
for (i, &b) in self.data.iter().enumerate().rev() {
    if b != 0 { last = Some(i * 8 + 7 - b.trailing_zeros() as usize); break; }
}
```

It is called once or twice per macroblock ([`h264/src/slicedec.rs:1454,1463`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/h264/src/slicedec.rs#L1454)).

**Scenario.** A slice NAL padded with 8 MB of zero bytes means 8,160 MBs × 8 MB, about 65 GB scanned per 1080p picture. `insert.video` decodes the poster synchronously in a command, which hangs the UI. Playback stalls the decode worker.

**Fix.** Compute the stop-bit position once, at reader construction or lazily in a `Cell<Option<usize>>`.

title: [Audit] Embedded font collection face count is uncapped
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-09 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Medium  
**Category:** DoS / memory  
**Confidence:** Plausible  
**Audit ID:** F-09

**Evidence.** [`fonts/src/fontdb.rs:609-616`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs#L609-L616):
```rust
let count = match FileRef::new(data) {
    Ok(FileRef::Font(_)) => 1,
    Ok(FileRef::Collection(c)) => c.len(),
```

Every face is built by `make_face`, harfrust shaper data included, before duplicates are removed. The system-font scan caps collections at `MAX_FACES = 256` ([`fontdb.rs:410,423`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs#L410)); the embedded path ([`engine/src/fonts.rs:13-21`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/engine/src/fonts.rs#L13-L21), parts ≤ 32 MiB) does not. A collection whose millions of offsets all point at one small font forces millions of face builds at open time. Named-instance dedupe is also O(n²).

**Fix.** `count.min(256)`, skip repeated table-directory offsets, and cap named instances per face.

title: [Audit] Metafile work escapes the budget
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-10 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Medium (CPU)  
**Category:** DoS / CPU  
**Confidence:** Confirmed (missing guard), cost estimated  
**Audit ID:** F-10

**Evidence.**

- [`metafile/src/canvas.rs:388-410`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/metafile/src/canvas.rs#L388-L410) (`push_raw`) returns before charging `cost` when the clip is empty.
- The expensive work has already happened by then: gradient tiles up to 129×129 cells × 256 stops (`canvas.rs:552-574`), nested-picture copies, and `clip_blit` of full bitmaps. A single EMF+ fill record may carry 50,000 rectangles.
- Separately, the [`emfplus.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/metafile/src/emfplus.rs) `region_node` path arm advances by the declared `size`, not by the bytes `path()` consumed. Sibling nodes can then re-read up to 100k points each; only the depth (32) is capped.

**Fix.** Keep a work counter separate from the output budget and charge it before doing work. Skip shading and bitmap work when the clip is empty. Make `path()` return the bytes it consumed and require `size >= consumed`.

title: [Audit] Video memory budget leaves out RGBA output and metadata
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-11 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Medium  
**Category:** DoS / memory  
**Confidence:** Plausible (arithmetic from code)  
**Audit ID:** F-11

`DECODE_MEMORY_BUDGET = 4 GiB` ([`bitstream/src/budget.rs:10`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/bitstream/src/budget.rs#L10)) counts YUV planes only. Not counted:

- RGBA frames in `sync_channel(AHEAD = 6)`, `current`/`next`, `ready`, and the UI `ColorImage`;
- motion and metadata arrays;
- the budget being per decoder: each playing video gets 4 GiB.

A legal 16384×8192 H.264 stream passes the budget (~2.4 GB) but needs ~4.3 GB of RGBA in flight, so it aborts on 8 to 16 GB machines.

**Fix.** Include RGBA × (AHEAD + 3) in the budget check at `VideoDecoder::open`, and downscale to ≤ 4096 px on the long side before RGBA conversion.

title: [Audit] Control server resource bounds are generous
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-12 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Low  
**Category:** DoS (local)  
**Confidence:** Confirmed  
**Audit ID:** F-12

> Related: #263 (control server authentication).

`Limits::default()` ([`control_server.rs:36-44`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/apps/deckcraft/src/control_server.rs#L36-L44)) is `max_line = 256 MiB`, `max_clients = 16`, `idle_timeout = 600 s`:

- 16 local clients × 256 MiB lines, plus a `serde_json::Value` copy each, is more than 8 GB.
- A client sending one byte every 599 s holds a slot indefinitely, so 16 such clients lock out the legitimate agent.

**Fix.** Lower `max_line` (stream base64 payloads or reference files by path), shorten the idle timeout, and with #263's token, refuse unauthenticated connections before buffering.

title: [Audit] `zip 3.0.0` advisories are not reachable today
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-13 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Low  
**Category:** Dependency advisory  
**Audit ID:** F-13

RUSTSEC-2026-0367/0368/0369 concern `ZipArchive::extract*` and `ZipStreamReader::extract`. The workspace uses only `ZipArchive::new`, `by_index`, `by_name`, `index_for_name`, `read_to_end` and `ZipWriter` ([`crates/format/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/format/src/lib.rs), [`crates/pptx/src/opc.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/pptx/src/opc.rs), [`pptx/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/pptx/src/lib.rs)), so none is reachable. Upgrade to `zip ≥ 9` anyway so audit gates stay green and the crate gets central-directory hardening. Add a `deny.toml` that ignores these IDs with a justification until then.

title: [Audit] Quadratic close-tag scan in HTML paste
author: PierrunoYT
body: Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4). **Severity:** Low **Category:** DoS / CPU **Confidence:** Needs verification (timing estimated) **Audit ID:** F-14 [`engine/src/cmd/richclip.rs:107-118`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/engine/src/cmd/richclip.rs#L107-L118): every closing tag does `stack.iter().rposition(|e| e.0 == kind)`, and the stack grows with each opening style tag. Input is capped at 1 MiB, but `` × 125k followed by `` × 125k gives about 1.6e10 comparisons, a freeze of seconds to tens of seconds on paste. The loop bound `runs <= MAX_RUNS` does not limit tag processing. **Fix.** Cap `stack.len()` (for example, 256), or keep per-kind counters instead of scanning.

title: [Audit] Spell-check has no word-length cap
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-15 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Low  
**Category:** DoS / CPU  
**Confidence:** Needs verification  
**Audit ID:** F-15

`Dictionary::check` → `check_exact` → `compounded()` ([`engine/src/spell.rs:307-330`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/engine/src/spell.rs#L307-L330)) loops over every split point, allocating a `String` for each head. Recursion is depth-limited to 8. `suggest()` is capped at 64 characters ([`spell.rs:390`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/engine/src/spell.rs#L390)), but `check()` is not. A 100k-character "word" in a deck costs O(n²) per check under a compounding dictionary (German, Dutch, …), and spell-check reruns on edits.

**Fix.** Treat words longer than about 100 characters as unchecked.

title: [Audit] AV1 header limits
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-16 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Low  
**Category:** DoS  
**Confidence:** Confirmed (missing checks)  
**Audit ID:** F-16

- Non-uniform tile spacing allows up to sb_cols × sb_rows tiles ([`av1/src/header.rs:898-927`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/av1/src/header.rs#L898-L927)). `MAX_TILE_COLS/ROWS` is enforced only for uniform spacing. Each `TileState` clones whole-frame LR/CDEF tables ([`state.rs:272`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/av1/src/state.rs#L272)), about 1 GB transient at 8K.
- The reference scaling ratio (`2*FrameWidth >= RefUpscaledWidth`, `FrameWidth <= 16*RefUpscaledWidth`) is not validated (`inter.rs:155-258`). This leads to i32 wraparound and an out-of-bounds index that `guarded()` catches: a CPU spike, not a crash.

**Fix.** Enforce both checks in `FrameHeader::parse`, as VP9 does ([`vp9/decoder.rs:316`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/vp9/src/decoder.rs#L316)).

title: [Audit] Release workflow passes signing secrets to an unpinned reusable workflow
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-17 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Low (documented design choice)  
**Category:** Supply chain  
**Audit ID:** F-17

[`.github/workflows/release.yml:21-42`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/.github/workflows/release.yml#L21-L42):

```yaml
uses: storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/release.yml@main
secrets:
  APPLE_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE }}
  ...
  AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET }}
```

Anyone able to push to `craft-common-actions@main` can exfiltrate the Apple, Windows and Azure signing credentials at the next release. The comment says this is intentional. Consider SHA-pinning the release workflow only, with Renovate or Dependabot bumps, and requiring signed commits and branch protection on `craft-common-actions`. Third-party actions in [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/.github/workflows/ci.yml) are already SHA-pinned.

author: PierrunoYT

title: [Audit] Panics outside the inner `catch_unwind` in `spawn_fifo` jobs abort the process
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-19 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Info  
**Category:** Robustness  
**Audit ID:** F-19

The rayon `spawn_fifo` jobs in [`h264/decoder.rs:560-590`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/h264/src/decoder.rs#L560-L590) and [`hevc/decoder.rs:553-590`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/hevc/src/decoder.rs#L553-L590) run `PicState::new`/`reset` and stats code outside their inner `catch_unwind`. title: [Audit] Manifest file paths go to `include_bytes!` unconstrained; a tampered craft-fonts checkout could embed arbitrary host files
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:F-22 -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Info  
**Category:** Build  
**Audit ID:** F-22

In [`crates/fonts/build.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/fonts/build.rs), the manifest's `file` column is `canonicalize()`d and passed to `include_bytes!` with no containment check. A tampered craft-fonts checkout could embed any readable build-host file (for example, CI secrets on disk) into released binaries. **Fix:** require the resolved path to start with `dir.canonicalize()`. The other build scripts are benign: [`ui-egui/build.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/ui-egui/build.rs) and [`apps/deckcraft/build.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/apps/deckcraft/build.rs) read `contributors/*` and write only to `OUT_DIR`, with string values emitted via `{:?}`.

title: [Audit] Minor robustness findings (grouped)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- deckcraft-audit:Minor -->
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [1dc69720db64](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4).

**Severity:** Info  
**Category:** various  
**Audit ID:** Minor

- **Debug-only overflow panics in codecs** (wrong output in release, memory-safe):
  - H.264 POC math: `slice.rs:435-470`.
  - H.264 MMCO and ref-list math: `dpb.rs:224,285,300`.
  - HEVC latency: `decoder.rs:425`.
  - HEVC POC math: `dpb.rs:163,174`.

  Use `wrapping_`/`saturating_` arithmetic or i64. Some of these run on the UI thread via #1166 in debug builds.
- **`BitReader::read_bits` / `peek`** with n > 32 is only `debug_assert`ed. No caller does this today; return `Err` for cheap hardening.
- **MCP stdio** ([`crates/mcp/src/server.rs:62-70`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/mcp/src/server.rs#L62-L70)) uses `input.lines()`, which has no line cap, and a non-UTF-8 line ends the server with an error. The client is trusted, so this is robustness only.
- **Metafile clip-region vectors** (`canvas.rs:392`) are not counted in `cost`: about 400 MB untracked at `MAX_ITEMS`.
- **WMF object-table scan** is O(4096) per record once full.
- **[`render/src/images.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/1dc69720db64323370dda061226becb09ad79fd4/crates/render/src/images.rs) `decode_raster`** skips the pre-decode dimension check when `into_dimensions()` fails. `image`'s default 512 MiB `max_alloc` still applies.

The write is atomic and does not follow symlinks (`io::write_file`), but another local user on Linux could swap the file between write and open. Use a per-user private temp dir.

title: [Feature Request] Please add official OpenCode skill support for DeckCraft
author: AHL8192
body:
Thanks for DeckCraft — the command engine is so complete that half of our deck-building code is just command ids and JSON.

DeckCraft is one of those rare apps where the agent surface is a first-class citizen rather than a bolted-on API: 321 commands in 31 namespaces, 25 MCP tools, a 960×540 pt slide model and `deckcraft-cli mcp` / attached mode both working. That is 90% of the work, and it is why this request is small.

## Why a skill, when the MCP server already exists?

An MCP server answers *"what can this app do?"*. A skill answers *"what should an agent do next, in what order, with which ids, and which footguns should it avoid?"*

The gap we kept falling into:

| Without a skill | With a skill |
|---|---|
| Command ids discovered by trial and error | Namespaces and ids named up front |
| Coordinates and units guessed | Conventions stated once, with the failure mode |
| Silent coercions quietly corrupt output | Known coercions listed, with the read-back that catches them |
| Every session re-derives the workflow | Verified recipes to copy |

MCP makes DeckCraft *possible* to drive. A skill makes it *reliable* to drive — in the same way your own docs do for a human.

## The ask

- [ ] **Ship the skill in-tree** — e.g. `.opencode/skills/deckcraft/SKILL.md` alongside `references/` and `scripts/`, versioned with the app
- [ ] **One line in the README** next to the MCP section saying how to install it
- [ ] **Regenerate the volatile bits at release** (version, tool count, command ids) — the included scripts do most of this already

## What we're handing over

title: Proposal: whole-slide Design Ideas (arrangement, colour and background in one click, offline)
author: xc4pr
body:
## Problem

Design Ideas moves and resizes a slide's shapes, but it keeps the slide's colours, background and type, so every idea reads as the same slide with its boxes moved. People expect what they know from other presentation apps (watched only as black-box behaviour): one click on an idea restyles the **whole** slide (arrangement, background and colour treatment together) and the content stays as it was. Slides with only a title get no ideas, and once #1200 lands, neither will slides with a table, chart or diagram.

## Today (0.10.0)

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/ideas.rs` (#314, #489) provides `design.ideas` and `design.applyIdea`. `roles()` finds the title, the largest picture and the text shapes. `ideas_for()` offers 4 picture arrangements or 3 text arrangements. `apply_idea()` writes explicit `xfrm`s, cover-crops the picture and sends it to the back. For `fullBleed` it fills the title with a fixed white (`Rgba::rgba(255, 255, 255, 220)`) that ignores the theme. Everything runs in one `Session::edit`, so it is one undo step, and the theme is untouched.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/panes.rs` `designer()` makes one thumbnail per idea: it calls `apply_idea` on a cloned deck and then `deckcraft_render::render_slide`. Thumbnails are cached in `IdeaThumbs`, keyed by (doc uid, revision, slide, width). The built-in themes follow as a whole-deck section (`design.theme`). `ideas_for()` runs every frame, so it must stay cheap.
- Fixes in flight: #1200 (only arrangeable shapes; slides with diagrams, tables or charts get no ideas), #1201 (the full-bleed band stays behind), #1202 (the button is clipped off the ribbon).
- Building blocks that already exist:
  - `Slide.color_map` (`clrMapOvr`). The PPTX reader and writer handle it and `resolve::Ctx::for_slide` resolves it. The default master background is `Background::Ref { idx: 1001, color: bg1 }` and placeholder text is `tx1`, so a slide colour map turns one slide dark without touching the master.

title: Format Painter: distinguish whole-shape clicks from double-click text selection
author: coderabbitai
body:
## Summary

Explore and implement gesture-aware Format Painter handling so a double-click on text in a shape that is not already open for text editing can paint the selected word instead of painting the whole shape on the first press.

Requested by @fchinu as a follow-up to PR #1076. This is an intentional behavior change to evaluate separately, not a regression introduced by that PR.

## Current behavior

In `crates/engine/src/tools.rs`, `Session::down` handles `Hit::Shape` by calling `format.painterApply` with the shape ID when Format Painter is armed. This paints the whole shape immediately and consumes a one-shot painter.

A subsequent double-click can select a word, but the one-shot painter is no longer armed. PR #1076 preserves this existing shape-click behavior and adds selection painting for text already being edited.

## Required changes

- Define how to distinguish a plain shape click from a double-click text-selection gesture before consuming the painter.
- Update the pointer gesture and painter application flow so a double-click on previously unedited text can apply copied formatting only to the selected word.
- Retain whole-shape painting for a confirmed plain click.
- Preserve one-shot and sticky painter semantics and existing text-editing selection behavior.
- Add regression tests for realistic pointer event sequences.

title: Web build: Office decks lose Arial, Times New Roman and Calibri (no metric-compatible stand-ins embedded)
author: realmarauder
body:
In the web build, `crates/fonts/build.rs` embeds only Inter and BIZ UDPGothic (the `if wasm && !matches!(…)` filter), so a .pptx set in Arial, Times New Roman, Calibri or Cambria is drawn entirely in the fallback font, even though `fontdb::substitutes` already maps those families to Liberation Sans, Liberation Serif, Carlito and Caladea. Lines break differently than in PowerPoint (text runs past its box), and the missing-fonts toast lists every one of them.

We build the web app with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` pointing at storytold/craft-fonts#8 (`fonts/latin-manifest.txt`, files checked against its SHA-256 sums) and let the web filter take those four families too:

```diff
-        if wasm && !matches!((*family, *style), ("BIZ UDPGothic", "Regular") | ("Inter", "Regular" | "Bold" | "Variable")) {
+        if wasm
+            && !matches!((*family, *style), ("BIZ UDPGothic", "Regular") | ("Inter", "Regular" | "Bold" | "Variable"))
+            && !matches!(*family, "Liberation Sans" | "Liberation Serif" | "Carlito" | "Caladea")
+        {
```

Decks then render at PowerPoint's widths in the browser. The cost is about 6 MB more inside the wasm, roughly 3 MB more over the wire (our release zip went from 11 MB to 14 MB). Given the web size budget, this may fit better behind a build option or as fonts fetched on demand than in the default build; happy to open a PR whichever way you prefer.

title: PPTX: a reopened video reports duration, width and height as 0
author: aiongg
body:
A video read from a `.pptx` has `MediaClip::duration_ms`, `width` and `height` at 0 ("unknown"). The `.pptx` reader doesn't probe the media bytes, which `insert.video` does.

Steps (main at c787f4f):

1. `deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'insert.video={"path":"clip.mp4"}' --cmd 'media.info={}' --print --save deck.pptx`
2. `deckcraft-cli run --in deck.pptx --cmd 'media.info={}' --print`

Step 1 reports `durationMs: 2023, width: 320, height: 240`. Step 2 reports `durationMs: 0, width: 0, height: 0`, while its `probe` has the right duration and size. The same happens with a `.mkv`, and with a 2 s H.264/AAC or VP9/Opus clip made by ffmpeg.

The player re-probes when playback starts (`ui-egui/src/media.rs:194`), but the media controls show a 0 duration before the first play (`media.rs:421`).

title: A PDF export that hangs on one core (fixed), and a 1.3–2.4× speed-up from swapping dependencies
author: Ttimmahlax
body:
Hi DeckCraft team 👋

We make software and hardware for home devices. While using DeckCraft we swapped some of our house
technology in underneath it: a faster allocator, and pure-Rust picture and audio codecs.

Two things came out of it. First, we found and fixed a hang in the renderer DeckCraft builds on.
Second, DeckCraft got noticeably faster, and a few other bugs turned up along the way. We're
reporting all three: the fix because it affects every DeckCraft user, the numbers in case they're
useful, and the bugs because you'll want them.

## The problem we fixed: PDF export can hang when DeckCraft gets one CPU core

With the process limited to one core, exporting a picture-heavy deck to PDF took anywhere from
5 s to forever. One run was still spinning after 2.4 hours. The same export with more cores takes
a few seconds.

**Cause.** The cause is in **vello_cpu**, not DeckCraft. `MultiThreadedDispatcher::flush` waits for
its worker threads by calling `try_recv()` in a loop, without blocking, yielding or sleeping.

- PDF export asks for 4 render threads (`crates/pdf/src/lib.rs:443`). When the process can use
  fewer cores than that, the spinning thread starves the workers it's waiting for.
- On Windows it was also boosted to priority 14, above the workers' 13.
- We read the stuck process's stacks: the main thread was Running in
  `try_recv` ← `record_finished_commands` ← `flush`, and the workers were Ready but never got the
  core.
- Widening the stuck process's affinity to 8 cores made it finish in 0.16 s.
- vello_cpu 0.3.0, the latest release, still spins.

**Fix.** One line: while flushing, block on `recv()` instead of spinning on `try_recv()`. Patched
and unpatched builds, alternated, 20 runs each, pinned to one core:

| build | min | median | max | never finished |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| unpatched | 5.5 s | 9.0 s | 22.1 s | 0/20 this session (up to 11/20 in others) |
| **patched** | **3.3 s** | **3.5 s** | **3.9 s** | **0/20** |

The PDFs are byte-identical. The…

title: mcp --connect: keep serving when the app isn't open yet (like lightcraft-cli)
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
When an MCP client (Claude Code) starts `deckcraft-cli mcp --connect 127.0.0.1:7979` while DeckCraft isn't running, the CLI exits at once ("can't reach the DeckCraft app… Connection refused"), so the client marks the server failed for its whole session; opening DeckCraft afterwards doesn't help until a manual reconnect.

`lightcraft-cli mcp --connect` already handles this: it answers `initialize`/`tools/list`, returns "not reachable… will retry on each call" for tool calls, and connects once the app's port opens. Could `deckcraft-cli` do the same (or offer a `--lazy` flag)? storytold/gridcraft#2280 proposes the suite-level version of this (a runtime `mcp.attach`), which would cover it too.

The two related MCP ideas (an Elicitation when the app is closed, and Tasks for long jobs) now have suite-wide tickets: storytold/wordcraft#4153 and storytold/wordcraft#4154.

**Repro:** close DeckCraft, add `deckcraft-cli mcp --connect 127.0.0.1:7979` as an MCP server in Claude Code, start a session: the server shows "failed" for the whole session.

**Environment:** Arch Linux, deckcraft-bin 0.10.0.

title: Linux XWayland: Vietnamese input garbled over XIM (same as wordcraft#2932)
author: nguyenphivn
body:
On Ubuntu 26.04 (GNOME, Wayland) DeckCraft runs through XWayland by default, so the input method talks to it over XIM. With a Vietnamese fcitx5 engine that fixes a word by forwarding BackSpace and then committing the new text, the slide text comes out garbled. It looks like the same bug as storytold/wordcraft#2932.

**Environment:** DeckCraft 0.10.0 (linux-x86_64 AppImage), Ubuntu 26.04 GNOME 50 Wayland, fcitx5 5.1.19, Ngó Sen 1.5.6 (https://github.com/ngosen/ngosen), Telex, default "Gõ Sen" mode (no preedit).

**Steps**
1. New presentation, click into the title placeholder.
2. Type the keys `tieengs vieetj cos daaus` (Telex for "tiếng việt có dấu").

**Expected:** `Tiếng việt có dấu`
**Actual:** wrong in 2 of 4 runs, e.g. `tiêiees viieej có dấu` and `Tiếng viieej có dấu`.

Keys were sent with `virsh send-key` at 150, 80, 150 and 50 ms between keys, and the title was read back through `--control` (`document.inspect`).

**Checks, same keys sent the same way**

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| Default (XWayland, XIM) | 2/4 correct |
| `DECKCRAFT_WAYLAND=1` (native Wayland) | 4/4 correct |
| XWayland, engine in preedit mode (no forwarded keys) | 3/3 correct |

**Likely cause:** `ime_output` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` sets `IMEOutput` from `ime_area`, which is the caret line while editing text, so the IME spot moves with every typed character. In WordCraft, @Nghiathan13 traced this to winit's X11 backend sending `XSetICValues(XNSpotLocation)` synchronously on each move; a BackSpace forwarded by the input method at that moment gets filtered by Xlib again and reaches the app late. The fix in storytold/wordcraft#3074 (leave the IME spot alone while typing over XIM, move it on a click or focus) would likely apply here too.

For comparison, DesignCraft 0.12.0 and LightCraft 0.13.0 also run through XWayland and typed the same keys correctly 4/4 in their text fields, so it is not every XIM client of the suite.

title: Shapes: the speech bubble's pointer isn't mirrored when its tip moves past the centre
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
The rectangular speech bubble ("Speech Bubble: Rectangle", `wedgeRectCallout`) and the rounded one (`wedgeRoundRectCallout`) draw their pointer at a different place depending on which side of the centre the tip is. On a 240×120 bubble with the tip below the box and left of the centre (adjust -10000, 80000), the pointer leaves the bottom edge at 2/12..5/12 of the width. Move the tip to the mirrored place on the right (10000, 80000) and it leaves at 5/12..9/12 (x 100..180), so the bubble is not the mirror image of the first one.

Expected: 7/12..10/12 (x 140..200), as presetShapeDefinitions gives it (`xg1 = ?: dxPos 7 2`, `xg2 = ?: dxPos 10 5`; the same for `yg1`/`yg2`). The same happens with the tip right of the box, below the centre instead of above it.

Cause: `wedge_rect` in `crates/geom/src/preset.rs` builds the far-side band from the near-centre one (5/12..7/12) and widens only its end, instead of using 7/12..10/12.

title: Shapes: "Arrow: Notched Right" draws its notch less than half as deep as it should be
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Insert "Arrow: Notched Right" (`notchedRightArrow`) at 200×100 with the default adjusts: the notch at the tail reaches x 11.25, so its edges are much flatter than the head's.

Expected: x 25. presetShapeDefinitions puts the notch point at `x1 = */ dy1 dx2 hd2` (the shaft's half height times the head length over half the height), so the notch edges run parallel to the head's edges. At 300×120 with adjusts (80000, 30000) that is 28.8.

Cause: `crates/geom/src/preset.rs` computes the notch as `dx * (k / 2.0) * 0.9`, an approximation instead of the guide formula.

title: Files: opening a Word RTF outline turns bulleted items into new slides titled "· text"
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Open an RTF outline saved by Word whose body points are a bulleted list. Each bulleted paragraph becomes a new slide titled "· Point" instead of a body point under the previous title.

Word writes each list item's bullet as a `{\listtext\pard\plain\f1\'b7\tab}` group right after the paragraph's `\li`. `rtf_to_outline` in `crates/format/src/rtf.rs` reads that group as text, so the bullet glyph lands in the line, and the `\pard` inside it resets the indent to 0, so the item is read as a title. Older writers' `{\pntext …}` group has the same glyph problem (the indent survives there because it has no `\pard`).

Expected: the item keeps its indent and its text, without the bullet: `\pard\fi-360\li720{\listtext\pard\plain\f1\'b7\tab}Point\par` reads as a level-2 point "Point".

Repro: `rtf_to_outline(r"{\rtf1\pard Title\par\pard\li720{\listtext\pard\plain\'b7\tab}Point\par}")` gives `"Title\n· Point\n"`.

title: Files: opening an RTF outline drops non-breaking hyphens
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Type "Year-end review" in Word with a non-breaking hyphen (Ctrl+Shift+-), save as RTF and open it in DeckCraft as an outline: the text reads "Yearend review".

Expected "Year‑end review", with the non-breaking hyphen (U+2011).

Cause: Word writes that hyphen as the control symbol `\_`. `rtf_to_outline` in `crates/format/src/rtf.rs` handles `\~` (non-breaking space) but not `\_`, so the hyphen is dropped.

Repro: `rtf_to_outline(r"{\rtf1 Year\_end\par}")` gives `"Yearend\n"`.

title: Files: saving as Outline/RTF drops every title paragraph after the first
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Type a slide title on two paragraphs (Enter in the title placeholder: "First line", then "Second line") and save the deck as Outline/RTF. The RTF contains only "First line"; "Second line" is gone. Saving as a plain-text outline keeps both, on one line.

Expected: the whole title in the RTF, still as one outline paragraph so it reopens as one slide.

Cause: `slides_to_rtf` in `crates/format/src/rtf.rs` writes only the first non-empty paragraph of the title (`paragraphs.iter().find(..)`).

title: Render/PDF: in Arabic text, the space beside a number moves to the wrong side and parentheses are reversed
author: jneaimi
body:
DeckCraft 0.10.0, CLI on Linux x86_64.

**What happens**

On a slide whose paragraphs are right-to-left (`format.rtl`), with Arabic text that mixes in Western digits and parentheses, DeckCraft's PNG preview and PDF misplace neutral characters:
- "تراجعت الإيرادات في أغسطس إلى 1,180,000 درهم" renders as "إلى  1,180,000درهم": the space after the number jumps to before it.
- "الإيرادات (درهم)", in a chart title and a table header, renders as "الإيرادات )درهم(": the parentheses are not mirrored, and they sit on the wrong side.

The saved PPTX text is correct (`rtl="1"`, in logical order): PowerPoint and LibreOffice draw it right. Only DeckCraft's renderer is wrong. It looks like the Unicode bidi rules for neutrals (N1/N2) and mirrored brackets (L4) are not applied around numbers.

**Repro**

A slide with a right-to-left bullet "الإيجار 420,000 درهم (سنوياً)". Render it with `render_slide`, or export a PDF.

**Expected**

The same visual order as PowerPoint: the space stays between the number and "درهم", and the brackets mirror.

title: CLI render: skip hidden slides (like PowerPoint's export) and accept --width
author: delosriosmedia
body:
## Summary

`deckcraft-cli render FILE --all OUT` draws hidden slides (`<p:sld show="0">`) too. PowerPoint's own export to pictures and PDF skips them, so a deck converted with DeckCraft gets extra slides the author hid on purpose.

## Repro (0.10.0, macOS CLI)

1. A 3-slide deck whose 2nd slide is hidden: `<p:sld show="0" …>` in `ppt/slides/slide2.xml`.
2. `deckcraft-cli render deck.pptx --all --scale 0.5 out/` writes `slide-01.png`, `slide-02.png` and `slide-03.png`.
3. `deckcraft-cli info deck.pptx` does report it: `slides[1].hidden == true`.

## Proposal

- `render --all` skips hidden slides, like PowerPoint's export, or gets a `--skip-hidden` flag if drawing them should stay the default. The output names could keep the slide number (`slide-01.png`, `slide-03.png`) so callers can map images back to slides.
- `render` accepts `--width PX`, like `render-transition` already does. Today the size comes from `--scale` in pixels per point, so a caller that needs 1920 px images has to read the slide size first and compute the scale.

## Why

We use `deckcraft-cli` as a headless converter in a church projection app ([Manna](https://github.com/delosriosmedia/manna)) to replace PowerPoint's export. Today we filter hidden slides ourselves with `info` before rendering, one `render --slide N` call per slide.

title: Bullets: an unavailable bullet font turns the bullet character into a generic dot (e.g. Noto Sans Symbols from Google Slides)
author: delosriosmedia
body:
## Summary

When a bullet's font isn't available, the bullet character is replaced by a generic dot instead of being drawn with a fallback font. Decks exported from Google Slides often use `Noto Sans Symbols` for bullets, so their `❑` and `❖` bullets all come out as `•`.

## Repro (0.10.0, macOS CLI; `Noto Sans Symbols` is not installed)

A text box with these three paragraphs (only the bullet font changes):

```xml
<a:p><a:pPr marL="457200" indent="-457200"><a:buFont typeface="Noto Sans Symbols"/><a:buChar char="❑"/></a:pPr><a:r><a:rPr lang="en-US" sz="3200"/><a:t>U+2751 in Noto Sans Symbols</a:t></a:r></a:p>
<a:p><a:pPr marL="457200" indent="-457200"><a:buFont typeface="Arial"/><a:buChar char="❑"/></a:pPr><a:r><a:rPr lang="en-US" sz="3200"/><a:t>U+2751 in Arial</a:t></a:r></a:p>
<a:p><a:pPr marL="457200" indent="-457200"><a:buFont typeface="Noto Sans Symbols"/><a:buChar char="❖"/></a:pPr><a:r><a:rPr lang="en-US" sz="3200"/><a:t>U+2756 in Noto Sans Symbols</a:t></a:r></a:p>
```

`deckcraft-cli render deck.pptx --slide 0 out.png` draws:

- line 1: `•` (expected `❑`);
- line 2: `❑` (correct: Arial lacks the glyph too, but the fallback finds it);
- line 3: `•` (expected `❖`).

Wingdings bullets (`buFont="Wingdings"`, `buChar="q"`) are fine.

## Expected

An unavailable bullet font is treated like an unavailable text font: the character is kept and drawn with the regular fallback chain. Swapping it for `•` should only happen when no font has the glyph.

Found while comparing real-world decks against PowerPoint for [Manna](https://github.com/delosriosmedia/manna), a church projection app; the repro above is synthetic.
