title: Animations approximate the preset instead of playing the behaviours stored in the file
author: Sassisasah
body:
_Found while comparing DeckCraft's rendering (core at 38d2ade) pixel by pixel with PowerPoint 16 on Windows 11 and macOS._

We built a deck with all 203 effects PowerPoint can create (53 entrance, 33 emphasis, 53 exit, 64 motion paths; one per slide, created by PowerPoint itself via COM) and compared DeckCraft frame by frame (10 fps) against PowerPoint's own video export of the same deck. With the preset approximations, 37 effects were clearly wrong:
- colour emphasis changes no colour (Darken, Lighten, Complementary Color 1/2, Contrasting Color, Desaturate, Brush On Color, Color Wave, Grow With Color, Change Font Color, Change Line Color, Blast)
- moving entrances/exits only fade (Zip, Credits, Crawl, Center Revolve, Sling, Float, Flip, Swivel, Light Speed, Pinwheel, Flash Once, Box)
- Bold Flash darkens the shape instead of bolding the text, Bounce (exit) takes another path
- some preset ids map to wrong names (presetID 24 is Darken, 25 Desaturate)

But every file spells out each effect completely in its timing tree: `p:anim` with keyframes and formulas over `#ppt_x`/`ppt_y`/`ppt_w`/`ppt_h`, `p:animScale`, `p:animRot`, `p:animClr` (HSL shifts or target colours on `fillcolor`, `stroke.color`, `style.color`), `p:animMotion`, `p:animEffect` filters and `p:set`.

**What we did:** read the behaviour nodes of each effect (begin, duration, repeat, autoRev, accel/decel, fill, `tmFilter`, keyframes with `fmla`, from/to/by) and play them in file order with a small formula evaluator (operators, sin/cos/sqrt/min/max, `pi`, `e`, `$`, `#ppt_x` = value at effect start, `ppt_x` = value after the previous behaviours). A finished behaviour keeps its end value while the effect runs (presets chain behaviours like that, e.g. Bounce). `p:animEffect` filters map to opacity, clip or inset (fade, wipe, slide, barn/box/circle/diamond/plus, strips). Wipe filters are named after the edge they leave from (`wipe(down)` reveals the bottom edge first); for exits (`transition="out"`) the directio…

title: Slide animation state is also applied to layout/master shapes with the same shape id
author: Sassisasah
body:
_Found while comparing DeckCraft's rendering (core at 38d2ade) pixel by pixel with PowerPoint 16 on Windows 11 and macOS._

Shape ids (`p:cNvPr/@id`) are only unique within one part. A slide shape and a layout or master shape often share an id (e.g. `id="4"`). In `deckcraft-render` (`Renderer::shape_at`), the animation state from `RenderOpts::state` is looked up by `ShapeId` for every shape, including the backdrop (layout and master shapes). So an emphasis effect on slide shape 4 also animates layout/master shape 4.

**Repro:** a layout with any shape whose `cNvPr id` equals the id of an animated shape on the slide (in our test deck: a footer text box on the master and a "Pulse" emphasis on a slide box, both id 4). In the show, the footer grows and moves together with the box.

**Fix we use** (works, minimal):
```rust
// set in_backdrop while drawing layout/master shapes
let st = if self.in_backdrop { ShapeState::default() } else { f.opts.state.map(|g| g(s.id)).unwrap_or_default() };
```
A cleaner fix would key animation state by (part, shape id), or make `ShapeId` unique across parts on import.

title: Auto-reverse written on behaviour nodes is ignored (Pulse/Grow-Shrink never shrinks back)
author: Sassisasah
body:
_Found while comparing DeckCraft's rendering (core at 38d2ade) pixel by pixel with PowerPoint 16 on Windows 11 and macOS._

PowerPoint writes "Auto-reverse" as `autoRev="1"` on the behaviour time node (`p:animScale/p:cBhvr/p:cTn`), not on the effect node. `deckcraft-pptx` (`read/timing.rs`, `animations()`) only reads `autoRev` on the effect node, so `Animation::auto_reverse` stays false and a Grow/Shrink with auto-reverse grows and holds.

```xml
<p:cTn presetID="6" presetClass="emph" presetSubtype="0" fill="hold" nodeType="clickEffect">
  <p:childTnLst><p:animScale>
    <p:cBhvr><p:cTn dur="500" autoRev="1" fill="hold"/><p:tgtEl><p:spTgt spid="4"/></p:tgtEl></p:cBhvr>
    <p:by x="130000" y="130000"/>
  </p:animScale></p:childTnLst>
</p:cTn>
```
Expected: 0.5 s to 130 %, 0.5 s back to 100 %. Actual: grows to 130 % and stays.

**Fix we use:** treat the effect as auto-reversing if all timed behaviour nodes below it (`cTn` with `dur > 1`) carry `autoRev="1"` (except `colorPulse`, which already reverses):
```rust
auto_reverse: c.bool("autoRev").unwrap_or(false) || (effect != "colorPulse" && behaviours_auto_reverse(c)),
```
(`repeatCount`, `accel`/`decel` can also sit on behaviour nodes. See https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/issues/1361 for the general approach.)

title: Fallback font for symbols differs from PowerPoint; bold is lost on fallback glyphs
author: Sassisasah

title: EMF+ dual metafiles: only the GDI fallback is played (logos incomplete)
author: Sassisasah
body:
_Found while comparing DeckCraft's rendering (core at 38d2ade) pixel by pixel with PowerPoint 16 on Windows 11 and macOS._

For *dual* EMF+ files (EMF+ header flag bit 0), `deckcraft-metafile` ignores the EMF+ records and plays the plain EMF records. PowerPoint draws metafiles with GDI+, which does the opposite: it plays the EMF+ records and skips the plain ones (except after EmfPlusGetDC). Office-made logos can have an incomplete GDI fallback: the EMF+ part draws a nested metafile (EmfPlusDrawImage of a Metafile object) that the fallback lacks. Result: a 4 kB company logo EMF (72 records, almost all EMF+ comments) showed only a short line instead of the logo.

**Fix we use:** the EMF+ header always enables EMF+ playback; in dual files the plain EMF records are only played after EmfPlusGetDC (`Plus::plays_gdi`). All metafile tests pass (one test renamed to `emfplus_dual_files_draw_the_emfplus_records_like_gdiplus`).
(Related but different: #327, EMF shown as missing-picture box.)

title: Charts: several chart XML settings are ignored (axes, gridlines, layout, title, data labels, pie)
author: Sassisasah
body:
_Found while comparing DeckCraft's rendering (core at 38d2ade) pixel by pixel with PowerPoint 16 on Windows 11 and macOS._

Found by comparing real-world charts pixel by pixel with PowerPoint (geometry measured via COM):

1. `c:tickLblPos val="none"` does not hide axis labels (only `c:delete` does).
2. Gridlines with `c:spPr/a:ln/a:noFill` are drawn.
3. `c:plotArea/c:layout/c:manualLayout` is ignored, both `layoutTarget="inner"` and the default outer.
4. Automatic plot layout: PowerPoint leaves about 11 pt at the sides (DeckCraft 4 % of the width) and makes the value-axis column as wide as the longest label measured in the chart font plus about half the font size (48.5 pt for "100,00%" at 12 pt).
5. Title: a long title runs on one line out of the chart. PowerPoint wraps it inside its own box (fits the longest line, centred), takes size and bold from the run `rPr` (not `defRPr`: 16 pt bold vs 18.62 pt), keeps about ¾ of the title size between title box and plot area, and uses the text box insets (0.1" / 0.05").
6. Data labels: always above the bar, without box, in axis font, and later bars paint over them. PowerPoint uses `c:dLblPos` (default centre for stacked bars), the label box from `c:dLbls/c:spPr`, size/bold/colour from `c:txPr` (series before group), and draws labels after all bars.
7. Missing points (`c:pt` absent from `numCache`, `dispBlanksAs="gap"`) get a "0" label. PowerPoint shows nothing.
8. Category names wrap based on an estimate from character count. PowerPoint wraps only when the measured width exceeds the category width.
9. Category axis line is always 0.75 pt grey. PowerPoint uses `c:catAx/c:spPr/a:ln`.
10. Pie charts: labels are always inside and show only the value. PowerPoint supports `showPercent`/`showCatName` with separator ("; " for `c:lang` de), `outEnd`/`bestFit` outside with leader lines, per-point `c:dLbl` with `manualLayout` offsets and `delete`, and rounds percentages so they sum to 100 % (3.48 % → 4 %). An inner `manualLayout` fixes …

title: Tiled SVG picture fills use the rendered size as tile size
author: Sassisasah
body:
_Found while comparing DeckCraft's rendering (core at 38d2ade) pixel by pixel with PowerPoint 16 on Windows 11 and macOS._

A shape filled with a tiled SVG (`a:blipFill` with `asvg:svgBlip` only, `a:tile tx="0" ty="0" sx="100000" sy="100000" algn="ctr"`) shows its pattern at the wrong scale and offset. `images::natural_size` returns `None` for SVG, so the tile takes the size of the raster decoded for the shape instead of the SVG's own `width`/`height` (at 96 dpi), and the centre alignment is computed for that wrong size.

**Fix we use:** `svg::natural_size` (from the usvg tree: `width`/`height`, else `viewBox`), used by `images::natural_size` for SVG. (Depends on SVG support, see #297.)

title: Media settings in the timing tree are not read; no way to draw video frames
author: Sassisasah
body:
_Found while comparing DeckCraft's rendering (core at 38d2ade) pixel by pixel with PowerPoint 16 on Windows 11 and macOS._

PowerPoint stores a video's/sound's volume, mute, Loop until Stopped, Hide While Not Playing and Play Full Screen in the slide's timing tree, not on the picture: `p:video`/`p:audio` → `p:cMediaNode vol="80000" mute="1" showWhenStopped="0"`, `p:cTn repeatCount="indefinite"`, `p:video fullScrn="1"`. The reader ignores these, so `MediaClip::volume` is always 1 and `loop_play`/`hide_while_not_playing` are always false; full-screen playback is unknown. A player that decodes video itself also has no way to hand the current frame to the renderer: a media shape always draws its poster.

Example where this matters: a slide with a small video, a full-slide "closing" picture made visible at slide start and `p:video fullScrn="1"`. PowerPoint plays the video full screen above everything; without `fullScrn` the video plays hidden under the picture.

**What we did:** `timing::media_settings` reads the `cMediaNode`s and writes volume (`vol`/100000, `mute` → 0), loop, hide and full-screen into the target's `MediaClip` (also inside groups). New `RenderOpts::video_frames` (`ShapeId` → `VideoFrame` from BGRA pixels) so a media shape draws the decoded frame with the poster's crop.

title: [Bug] Left sidebar slide thumbnails do not auto-scroll or follow active selection when navigating via arrow keys in editor view
author: PunishedSnake90
body:
Environment

• OS: Linux Mint 22.3

Description

When navigating through slides in the main editor canvas using the arrow keys, the active slide transitions correctly, but the focus and scroll position of the left thumbnail sidebar does not update.

Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a presentation with enough slides to require vertical scrolling in the left sidebar.
2. Click on the main editor canvas or select a slide.
3. Use the keyboard arrow keys to move to the next slides.
4. Continue past the visible bounds of the left sidebar.

Expected Behavior

The left sidebar thumbnail rail should dynamically track the active slide selection and auto-scroll (scroll-into-view) so that the currently active slide thumbnail remains visible to the user.

Actual Behavior

The main canvas changes slides, but the left thumbnail bar stays static, requiring manual mouse scrolling or clicking to see where you are in the list.

title: [macOS] ⌘Q exits immediately with unsaved changes without prompting to save
author: piyushgoel2808
body:
### Summary
On macOS, pressing **⌘Q** (or selecting Quit from the application menu) immediately terminates DeckCraft and loses any unsaved changes in dirty presentations.

In contrast, clicking the window close button (`X`) properly intercepts the close request, checks if any document is dirty (`self.session.documents().iter().any(|d| d.is_dirty())`), and displays the `"quit"` confirmation dialog asking the user whether to Save, Don't Save, or Cancel (`egui::ViewportCommand::CancelClose`).

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch DeckCraft on macOS.
2. Create a new presentation or open an existing presentation.
3. Make an edit (e.g. add a shape or type text) so the presentation has unsaved modifications.
4. Press **⌘Q** on the keyboard.
5. **Observed**: The application terminates immediately; unsaved changes are lost.
6. **Expected**: DeckCraft should prompt the user to save changes (the same prompt that appears when clicking the window close button).

### Root Cause
On macOS, `winit` handles `⌘Q` / `[NSApp terminate:]` by terminating the event loop and exiting the process directly, bypassing egui's `close_requested()` event.

### Proposed Solution
Intercept `⌘Q` on macOS so that it routes through `egui::ViewportCommand::Close`, allowing DeckCraft's existing unsaved-changes check in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` to prompt the user before closing.

title: [Feature Request] Quick Access Toolbar: support Alt+1..9 keyboard shortcuts for pinned items
author: piyushgoel2808
body:
### Summary
In the desktop presentation editor, items pinned to the Quick Access Toolbar (QAT) should be triggerable via sequential `Alt+1` through `Alt+9` keyboard shortcuts matching their position on the toolbar (position 1 = Alt+1, position 2 = Alt+2, ..., position 9 = Alt+9).

Currently, DeckCraft allows pinning and unpinning commands to the Quick Access Toolbar (`crates/ui-egui/src/qat.rs`), but pressing `Alt+1`..`Alt+9` does not execute the pinned tools.

### Expected Behavior
- When the presentation editor has focus and no modal dialog or text edit is active, pressing `Alt+1` through `Alt+9` should execute the corresponding Quick Access Toolbar tool at that 1-based index.
- If fewer tools are pinned than the pressed digit (e.g., pressing Alt+5 when only 3 tools are pinned), the key event is unhandled.
- Tooltips for the first 9 QAT buttons should indicate their `Alt+<N>` shortcut.
